sentences.zh: 【晉紀二十八】 起旃蒙作噩，盡柔兆閹茂，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 28] From Zhanmeng Zuoe through Rouzhao Yanmao; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals 28] From Zhanmeng Zuoe through Rouzhao Yanmao—two years in all.

translations.literal: From the middle section of Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong line, Taixuan year 10 (
translations.idiomatic: From the middle portion of Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong line, Taixuan year 10 (

translations.literal: yiyou, CE 385)
translations.idiomatic: yiyou, CE 385)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，秦王堅朝饗群臣，時長安饑，人相食，諸將歸，吐肉以飼妻子。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, King Fu Jian of Qin held court and feasted his ministers. At that time Chang'an was stricken with famine and men ate one another; when the generals returned home, they spat out meat to feed their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, King Fu Jian of Qin held court and entertained his ministers. Chang'an was then in famine, and people were eating one another; when the generals returned home, they would spit out meat to feed their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖即皇帝位於阿房，改元更始。

translations.literal: Murong Chong declared himself emperor at Epang and changed the era name to Gengshi.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong declared himself emperor at Epang and proclaimed the era name Gengshi.

sentences.zh: 沖有自得之志，賞罰任情。

translations.literal: Chong was self-satisfied in spirit, and rewards and punishments followed his whim.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had grown complacent, meting out rewards and punishments entirely on whim.

sentences.zh: 慕容盛年十三，謂慕容柔曰：「夫十人之長，亦須才過九人，然後得安。

translations.literal: Murong Sheng, aged thirteen, said to Murong Rou: "As leader of ten men, one's talent must surpass that of nine others before one can remain secure.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Sheng, only thirteen years old, said to Murong Rou, "To lead ten men, your abilities must exceed those of nine others—only then can you hold your position securely.

sentences.zh: 今中山王才逮人，功未有成，而驕汰已甚，殆難濟乎！」

translations.literal: Now the Prince of Zhongshan is merely equal to other men in talent; his achievements are not yet accomplished, yet he is already excessively arrogant and extravagant—will he not be hard put to succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Our Prince of Zhongshan is barely a match for ordinary men; his success is far from assured, yet he is already insufferably arrogant and extravagant. I fear he will not prevail!"

sentences.zh: 後秦王萇留諸將攻新平，自引兵擊安定，擒秦安西將軍勃海公珍，嶺北諸城悉降之。

translations.literal: Later Qin King Yao Chang left his generals to attack Xinping and personally led troops to strike Anding, capturing the Former Qin Anxi General, Duke of Bohai, Zhen; all the cities north of the ridges submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin king Yao Chang left his generals to besiege Xinping and personally marched against Anding, capturing the Former Qin Anxi general, the Duke of Bohai, Zhen, after which all cities north of the ridges surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，秦王堅與西燕主沖戰於仇班渠，大破之。

translations.literal: On jiayin, King Fu Jian of Qin fought the Western Yan ruler Murong Chong at Qiuban Qu and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, King Fu Jian of Qin met Western Yan ruler Murong Chong at Qiuban Qu and routed him.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，戰於雀桑，又破之。

translations.literal: On yimao, they fought at Quesang and he defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao they fought at Quesang, and Fu Jian won again.

sentences.zh: 甲子，戰於白渠，秦兵大敗。

translations.literal: On jiazi, they fought at Bai Qu and the Qin army suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi they fought at Bai Qu, and the Qin army was routed.

sentences.zh: 西燕兵圍秦王堅，殿中將軍鄧邁等力戰卻之，堅乃得免。

translations.literal: Western Yan troops surrounded King Fu Jian; Palace Attendant General Deng Mai and others fought fiercely and drove them back, and Fu Jian thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Western Yan troops surrounded King Fu Jian; Palace Attendant General Deng Mai and others fought fiercely to drive them off, and Fu Jian escaped.

sentences.zh: 壬申，沖遣尚書令高蓋夜襲長安，入其南城，左將軍竇沖、前禁將軍李辯等擊破之，斬首八百級，分其屍而食之。

translations.literal: On renshen, Chong sent Minister Over the Masses Gao Gai to raid Chang'an by night; they entered its southern city. Left General Dou Chong, Former Prohibited General Li Bian, and others defeated them, beheading eight hundred; they divided the corpses and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Chong sent Minister Over the Masses Gao Gai to raid Chang'an by night and enter its southern quarter. Left General Dou Chong, Former Prohibited General Li Bian, and others routed the attackers, beheading eight hundred men, whose corpses they divided and ate.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，高蓋引兵攻渭北諸壘，太子宏與戰於成貳壁，大破之，斬首三萬。

translations.literal: On yihai, Gao Gai led troops to attack the stockades north of the Wei; Crown Prince Hong fought him at Chengerbi and inflicted a great defeat, beheading thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Gao Gai marched against the stockades north of the Wei. Crown Prince Hong met him at Chengerbi, routed his army, and beheaded thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 燕帶方王佐與寧朔將軍平規共攻薊，王永兵屢敗。

translations.literal: Yan Prince of Daifang Zuo and Ningshuo General Ping Gui jointly attacked Ji; Wang Yong's army was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Prince of Daifang Zuo and Ningshuo General Ping Gui jointly attacked Ji, and Wang Yong's forces suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 二月，永使宋敞燒和龍及薊城宮室，帥眾三萬奔壺關；

translations.literal: In the second month, Yong had Song Chang burn Helong and the palaces of Ji city, then led thirty thousand men in flight to Huguan;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Yong had Song Chang burn Helong and the palaces of Ji, then led thirty thousand men in flight toward Huguan;

sentences.zh: 佐等入薊。

translations.literal: Zuo and the others entered Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo and his forces entered Ji.

sentences.zh: 慕容農引兵會慕容麟於中山，與共攻翟真。

translations.literal: Murong Nong led troops to join Murong Lin at Zhongshan, and together they attacked Zhai Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong led troops to join Murong Lin at Zhongshan, and together they attacked Zhai Zhen.

sentences.zh: 麟、農先帥數千騎至承營，觀察形勢。

translations.literal: Lin and Nong first led several thousand horsemen to Chengying to observe the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and Nong first led several thousand horsemen to Chengying to reconnoiter the situation.

sentences.zh: 翟真望見，陳兵而出。

translations.literal: Zhai Zhen saw them and deployed his troops to come out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Zhen saw them and marched out with his troops deployed for battle.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲退，農曰：「丁零非不勁勇，而翟真懦弱，今簡精銳，望真所在而沖之，真走，眾必散矣，乃邀門而蹙之，可盡殺也。」

translations.literal: The generals wished to withdraw. Nong said: "The Dingling are not lacking in fierce valor, but Zhai Zhen is timid. Now select elite troops, charge toward wherever Zhen is, and when Zhen flees the masses will surely scatter; then block the gates and press them—we can kill them all."
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to pull back. Nong said, "The Dingling are not without fierce valor, but Zhai Zhen is timid. Select elite troops now, charge straight at wherever Zhen stands, and when he flees his men will scatter. Then block the gates and crush them—we can wipe them out."

sentences.zh: 使驍騎將軍慕容國帥百餘騎沖之，真走，其眾爭門，自相蹈藉，死者太半；

translations.literal: He sent Valiant Cavalry General Murong Guo to lead a little more than a hundred horsemen in a charge; Zhen fled, and his men scrambled for the gates, trampling one another—more than half died;
translations.idiomatic: He sent Valiant Cavalry General Murong Guo at the head of a little more than a hundred horsemen to charge. Zhen fled, and his men fought for the gates, trampling one another to death—more than half perished;

sentences.zh: 遂拔承營外郭。

translations.literal: they then took the outer wall of Chengying.
translations.idiomatic: and they then captured the outer wall of Chengying.

sentences.zh: 癸未，秦王堅與西燕主沖戰於城西，大破之，追奔至阿城。

translations.literal: On guiwei, King Fu Jian of Qin fought the Western Yan ruler Murong Chong west of the city and inflicted a great defeat, pursuing the fugitives to Acheng.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, King Fu Jian of Qin fought Western Yan ruler Murong Chong west of the city, routed him, and pursued the fugitives to Acheng.

sentences.zh: 諸將請乘勝入城，堅恐為沖所掩，引兵還。

translations.literal: The generals asked to enter the city on the momentum of victory, but Fu Jian feared being ambushed by Chong and led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: The generals urged pressing the victory by entering the city, but Fu Jian feared an ambush by Chong and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，秦益州刺史王廣以蜀人江陽太守李丕為益州刺史，守成都。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Former Qin Inspector of Yizhou Wang Guang appointed the native of Shu, Administrator of Jiangyang Li Pi, as Inspector of Yizhou to hold Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Former Qin inspector of Yizhou Wang Guang appointed Li Pi, a native of Shu and administrator of Jiangyang, as inspector of Yizhou to hold Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 己丑，廣帥所部奔還隴西，依其兄秦州刺史統，蜀人隨之者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: On jichou, Guang led his command in flight back to Longxi, relying on his elder brother, Inspector of Qinzhou Tong; more than thirty thousand men of Shu followed him.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Guang led his command in flight back to Longxi to join his elder brother, Inspector of Qinzhou Tong, and more than thirty thousand men of Shu followed him.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之至枋頭。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi reached Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi reached Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 楊膺、姜讓謀洩，長樂公丕收殺之。

translations.literal: Yang Ying and Jiang Rang's plot was exposed; Prince of Changle Fu Pi arrested and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ying and Jiang Rang's plot was exposed, and Prince of Changle Fu Pi arrested and executed them.

sentences.zh: 牢之聞之，盤桓不進。

translations.literal: When Laozhi heard of it, he lingered and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Laozhi heard of it, he lingered and refused to advance.

sentences.zh: 秦平原悼公暉數為西燕主沖所敗，秦王堅讓之曰：「汝，吾之才子也，擁大眾與白虜小兒戰，而屢敗，何用生為！」

translations.literal: Former Qin Duke of Pingyuan, posthumous name Zhao, Fu Hui had been repeatedly defeated by the Western Yan ruler Murong Chong. King Fu Jian of Qin reproached him, saying: "You are my gifted son, yet you command a great host against the white-barbarian stripling and are repeatedly defeated—of what use is your life!"
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin Duke of Pingyuan, posthumous name Zhao, Fu Hui had been repeatedly defeated by Western Yan ruler Murong Chong. King Fu Jian reproached him, saying, "You are my gifted son, yet you lead a great army against that white-barbarian stripling and lose again and again—what use is your life!"

sentences.zh: 三月，暉憤恚自殺。

translations.literal: In the third month, Hui, in grief and rage, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Hui killed himself in grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 前禁將軍李辯、都水使者隴西彭和正恐長安不守，召集西州人屯於韭園；

translations.literal: Former Prohibited General Li Bian and Director of Waterways, Longxi native Peng Hezheng, fearing that Chang'an could not be held, gathered men of the western provinces and encamped them at Jiuyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Former Prohibited General Li Bian and Director of Waterways Peng Hezheng of Longxi, fearing Chang'an could not be held, gathered men of the western provinces and encamped them at Jiuyuan;

sentences.zh: 堅召之，不至。

translations.literal: Fu Jian summoned them, but they did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian summoned them, but they did not come.

sentences.zh: 西燕主沖攻秦高陽愍公方於驪山，殺之，執秦尚書韋鐘，以其子謙為馮翊太守，使招集三輔之民。

translations.literal: The Western Yan ruler Murong Chong attacked Former Qin Duke of Gaoyang, posthumous name Min, Fu Fang at Lishan, killed him, seized Former Qin Minister of the Masters of Writing Wei Zhong, and appointed his son Qian as Administrator of Fengyi to gather the people of the Three Adjuncts.
translations.idiomatic: Western Yan ruler Murong Chong attacked Former Qin Duke of Gaoyang, posthumous name Min, Fu Fang at Lishan and killed him. He seized Former Qin Minister of the Masters of Writing Wei Zhong and appointed Zhong's son Qian administrator of Fengyi to rally the people of the Three Adjuncts.

sentences.zh: 馮詡壘主邵安民等責謙曰：「君雍州望族，今乃從賊，與之為不忠不義，何面目以行於世乎？」

translations.literal: Stockade master of Fengyi Shao Anmin and others reproached Qian, saying: "Sir, you are a leading clan of Yongzhou—how can you now follow the rebels and join them in disloyalty and injustice? With what face can you walk in the world?"
translations.idiomatic: Stockade master of Fengyi Shao Anmin and others reproached Qian, saying, "Sir, you are a leading family of Yongzhou—how can you now follow the rebels and join them in disloyalty and injustice? With what face can you walk in the world?"

sentences.zh: 謙以告鐘，鐘自殺，謙來奔。

translations.literal: Qian told Zhong, and Zhong killed himself; Qian came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qian told Zhong, and Zhong killed himself; Qian then came over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 秦左將軍苟池、右將軍俱石子與西燕主沖戰於驪山，兵敗。

translations.literal: Former Qin Left General Gou Chi and Right General Ju Shizi fought the Western Yan ruler Murong Chong at Lishan and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin Left General Gou Chi and Right General Ju Shizi fought Western Yan ruler Murong Chong at Lishan and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 西燕將軍慕容永斬苟池，俱石子奔鄴。

translations.literal: Western Yan General Murong Yong beheaded Gou Chi; Ju Shizi fled to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Western Yan general Murong Yong beheaded Gou Chi, and Ju Shizi fled to Ye.

sentences.zh: 永，廆弟運之孫；

translations.literal: Yong was the grandson of Murong Hui's younger brother Yun;
translations.idiomatic: Yong was the grandson of Murong Hui's younger brother Yun;

sentences.zh: 石子，難之弟也。

translations.literal: Shizi was the younger brother of Murong Nanch.
translations.idiomatic: Shizi was the younger brother of Murong Nanch.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅遣領軍將軍楊定擊沖，大破之，虜鮮卑萬餘人而還，悉坑之。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin sent Commandant of the Guards Yang Ding to attack Chong and inflicted a great defeat, capturing more than ten thousand Xianbei and returning; he buried them all alive.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian sent Commandant of the Guards Yang Ding against Chong, routed him, captured more than ten thousand Xianbei, and on his return buried them all alive.

sentences.zh: 定，佛奴之孫，堅之婿也。

translations.literal: Ding was the grandson of Fu Fonu and Fu Jian's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was the grandson of Fu Fonu and Fu Jian's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 滎陽人鄭燮以郡來降。

translations.literal: Zheng Xie of Xingyang surrendered the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xie of Xingyang surrendered the commandery.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂攻鄴，久不下，將北詣冀州，乃命撫軍大將軍麟屯信都，樂浪王溫屯中山，召驃騎大將軍農還鄴；

translations.literal: Yan King Murong Chui attacked Ye but could not take it for a long time. He was about to go north to Jizhou and therefore ordered Pacification Army Grand General Lin to encamp at Xindu, Prince of Langye Wen to encamp at Zhongshan, and summoned Flying Cavalry Grand General Nong back to Ye;
translations.idiomatic: Yan king Murong Chui besieged Ye for a long time without taking it. About to march north to Jizhou, he ordered Pacification Army grand general Lin to encamp at Xindu, Prince of Langye Wen to encamp at Zhongshan, and summoned Flying Cavalry grand general Nong back to Ye;

sentences.zh: 於是遠近聞之，以燕為不振，頗懷去就。

translations.literal: When near and far heard of this, they took Yan to be in decline and many considered whether to stay or leave.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread near and far, people took Yan to be in decline, and many began weighing whether to stay or leave.

sentences.zh: 農至高邑，遣從事中郎眭邃近出，違期不還。

translations.literal: When Nong reached Gaoyi, he sent Attendant Gentleman Sui Sui on a mission nearby; Sui failed to return by the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: When Nong reached Gaoyi, he sent Attendant Gentleman Sui Sui on a nearby mission, but Sui failed to return by the appointed time.

sentences.zh: 長史張攀言於農曰：「邃目下參佐，敢欺罔不還，請回軍計之。」

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Zhang Pan said to Nong: "Sui is a subordinate under your eyes, yet he dares to deceive you and not return—please turn the army back to deal with this."
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Zhang Pan said to Nong, "Sui is a subordinate under your very eyes, yet he dares deceive you and not return—please turn the army back and deal with this."

sentences.zh: 農不應，敕備假版，以邃為高陽太守，參佐家在趙北者，悉假署遣歸。

translations.literal: Nong did not reply. He ordered provisional seals prepared, appointed Sui Administrator of Gaoyang, and for all subordinates whose families were in northern Zhao, he issued provisional appointments and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: Nong did not reply. He ordered provisional seals prepared, appointed Sui administrator of Gaoyang, and for every subordinate whose family was in northern Zhao he issued provisional appointments and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 凡舉補太守三人，長史二十餘人，退謂攀曰：「君所見殊誤，當今豈可自相魚肉！

translations.literal: In all he recommended and appointed three administrators and more than twenty chief clerks. He then withdrew and said to Pan: "Your view is quite mistaken—how can we now tear one another apart like fish and flesh!
translations.idiomatic: In all he recommended three administrators and more than twenty chief clerks. Then he withdrew and told Pan, "Your view is quite mistaken—how can we tear one another apart at a time like this!

sentences.zh: 俟吾北還，邃等自當迎於道左，君但觀之。」

translations.literal: Wait until I return north—Sui and the others will surely come to welcome me on the left of the road; you need only watch."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until I return north—Sui and the others will surely come to welcome me along the road. You need only watch."

sentences.zh: 樂浪王溫在中山，兵力甚弱，丁零四布，分據諸城。

translations.literal: Prince of Langye Wen was at Zhongshan with very weak forces; Dingling were scattered everywhere, each holding separate cities.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Langye Wen was at Zhongshan with very weak forces; Dingling bands were scattered everywhere, each holding separate cities.

sentences.zh: 溫謂諸將曰：「以吾之眾，攻則不足，守則有餘。

translations.literal: Wen said to the generals: "With our numbers, we are insufficient to attack but more than enough to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Wen told his generals, "With our numbers we are too few to attack but more than enough to defend.

sentences.zh: 驃騎、撫軍，首尾連兵，會須滅賊，但應聚糧厲兵以俟時耳。」

translations.literal: The Flying Cavalry and Pacification armies, front and rear linked in force, will surely have to destroy the bandits—we need only gather grain and sharpen weapons to await the time."
translations.idiomatic: The Flying Cavalry and Pacification armies, front and rear linked in force, will surely destroy the enemy—we need only gather grain and sharpen weapons and await the moment."

sentences.zh: 於是撫舊招新，勸課農桑，民歸附者相繼，郡縣壁壘爭送軍糧，倉庫充溢。

translations.literal: Thereupon he comforted the old and recruited the new, encouraged agriculture and sericulture, and people who submitted came in succession; commanderies, counties, and stockades vied to send army grain, and the storehouses overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he comforted the old and recruited the new, encouraged farming and sericulture, and people submitted in succession; commanderies, counties, and stockades vied to send army grain until the storehouses overflowed.

sentences.zh: 翟真夜襲中山，溫擊破之，自是不敢復至。

translations.literal: Zhai Zhen raided Zhongshan by night; Wen defeated him, and from then on he did not dare come again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Zhen raided Zhongshan by night; Wen defeated him, and from then on Zhai did not dare return.

sentences.zh: 溫乃遣兵一萬運糧以餉垂，且營中山宮室。

translations.literal: Wen then sent ten thousand troops to transport grain to supply Chui, and also built the palaces of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen then sent ten thousand troops to transport grain to supply Chui and began building the palaces of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之攻燕黎陽太守劉撫於孫就柵，燕王垂留慕容農守鄴圍，自引兵救之。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi attacked Yan Administrator of Liyang Liu Fu at Sunjiu Stockade. Yan King Murong Chui left Murong Nong to hold the siege of Ye and personally led troops to rescue Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi attacked Yan administrator of Liyang Liu Fu at Sunjiu Stockade. Yan king Murong Chui left Murong Nong to maintain the siege of Ye and personally led troops to rescue Fu.

sentences.zh: 秦長樂公丕聞之，出兵乘虛夜襲燕營，農擊敗之。

translations.literal: Former Qin Prince of Changle Fu Pi heard of this and led troops out to take advantage of the opening and raid the Yan camp by night; Nong defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin Prince of Changle Fu Pi heard of this and led troops out to raid the Yan camp by night while they were exposed; Nong defeated him.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之與垂戰，不勝，退屯黎陽。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi fought Chui but did not prevail and withdrew to encamp at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi fought Chui but could not prevail and withdrew to encamp at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 垂復還鄴。

translations.literal: Chui returned again to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Chui then returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 呂光以龜茲饒樂，欲留居之。

translations.literal: Lü Guang, finding Kucha rich and pleasant, wished to remain and dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Kucha rich and pleasant, Lü Guang wished to remain there.

sentences.zh: 天竺沙門鳩摩羅什謂光曰：「此凶亡之地，不足留也。

translations.literal: The Indian monk Kumarajiva said to Guang: "This is a place of violent ruin—not fit to remain.
translations.idiomatic: The Indian monk Kumarajiva told Guang, "This is a place of violent ruin—not fit to remain.

sentences.zh: 將軍但東歸，中道自有福地可居。」

translations.literal: General, you need only return east; along the way there will surely be a blessed land where you may dwell."
translations.idiomatic: General, you need only return east; along the way you will surely find a blessed land where you may dwell."

sentences.zh: 光乃大饗將士，議進止，眾皆欲還。

translations.literal: Guang then held a great feast for his officers and men to discuss whether to advance or withdraw; all wished to return.
translations.idiomatic: Guang then held a great feast for his officers and men to discuss whether to advance or withdraw, and all wished to return.

sentences.zh: 乃以駝二萬餘頭載外國珍寶奇玩，驅駿馬萬餘匹而還。

translations.literal: He then used more than twenty thousand camels to carry foreign treasures and curios, and drove more than ten thousand thoroughbred horses back.
translations.idiomatic: He then loaded more than twenty thousand camels with foreign treasures and curios and drove more than ten thousand thoroughbred horses homeward.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，劉牢之進兵至鄴。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Liu Laozhi advanced his army to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Liu Laozhi advanced his army to Ye.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂逆戰而敗；

translations.literal: Yan King Murong Chui met him in battle and was defeated;
translations.idiomatic: Yan king Murong Chui met him in battle and was defeated;

sentences.zh: 遂撤圍，退屯新城；

translations.literal: he then lifted the siege and withdrew to encamp at Xincheng;
translations.idiomatic: he then lifted the siege and withdrew to encamp at Xincheng;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，自新城北遁。

translations.literal: on yimao he fled north from Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: on yimao he fled north from Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 牢之不告秦長樂公丕，即引兵追之。

translations.literal: Laozhi, without informing Former Qin Prince of Changle Fu Pi, immediately led troops in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Without informing Former Qin Prince of Changle Fu Pi, Laozhi immediately led troops in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 丕聞之，發兵繼進。

translations.literal: When Pi heard of it, he sent troops to follow in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi heard of it, he sent troops to follow in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 庚申，牢之追及垂於董唐淵。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Laozhi caught up with Chui at Dongtang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Laozhi caught up with Chui at Dongtang Yuan.

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「秦、晉瓦合，相待為強。

translations.literal: Chui said: "Qin and Jin are joined like tiles and mortar, each relying on the other for strength.
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "Qin and Jin are joined like tiles and mortar, each relying on the other for strength.

sentences.zh: 一勝則俱豪，一失則俱潰，非同心也。

translations.literal: One victory and both prosper; one defeat and both collapse—they are not of one heart.
translations.idiomatic: One victory and both prosper; one defeat and both collapse—they are not of one heart.

sentences.zh: 今兩軍相繼，勢既未合，宜急擊之。」

translations.literal: Now the two armies are following one another in succession; their strength is not yet united—you should strike them quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Now the two armies are following one another in succession; their strength is not yet united—you should strike them quickly."

sentences.zh: 牢之軍疾趨二百里，至五橋澤，爭燕輜重；

translations.literal: Laozhi's army hurried two hundred li to Wuqiao Ze and scrambled for Yan baggage trains;
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi's army hurried two hundred li to Wuqiao Ze and scrambled for Yan baggage trains;

sentences.zh: 垂邀擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Chui intercepted and attacked, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Chui intercepted and attacked, inflicting a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Several thousand heads were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 牢之單馬走，會秦救至，得免。

translations.literal: Laozhi fled alone on horseback; when Qin relief arrived, he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi fled alone on horseback; when Qin relief arrived, he escaped.

sentences.zh: 燕冠軍將軍宜都王鳳每戰，奮不顧身。

translations.literal: Yan Champion General Prince of Yidu Feng fought in every battle, reckless of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Champion General Prince of Yidu Feng fought in every battle reckless of his life.

sentences.zh: 前後大小二百五十七戰，未嘗無功。

translations.literal: In two hundred fifty-seven engagements great and small, before and after, he never failed to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: In two hundred fifty-seven engagements great and small, he never failed to win distinction.

sentences.zh: 垂戒之曰：「今大業甫濟，汝當先自愛！」

translations.literal: Chui admonished him, saying: "The great enterprise has only just crossed— you must first cherish yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Chui admonished him, saying, "The great enterprise has only just crossed the ford—you must first cherish yourself!"

sentences.zh: 使為車騎將軍德之副，以抑其銳。

translations.literal: He made him deputy to General of Chariots and Cavalry De to restrain his keen edge.
translations.idiomatic: He made him deputy to General of Chariots and Cavalry De to restrain his keen edge.

sentences.zh: 鄴中饑甚，秦長樂公丕帥眾就晉谷於枋頭。

translations.literal: Famine in Ye was severe; Former Qin Prince of Changle Fu Pi led his masses to obtain Jin grain at Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Famine in Ye was severe; Former Qin Prince of Changle Fu Pi led his men to obtain Jin grain at Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之入屯鄴城，收集亡散，兵復少振；

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi entered and encamped in Ye city, gathering the scattered fugitives, and his army recovered somewhat;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi entered and encamped in Ye, gathered the scattered fugitives, and his army recovered somewhat;

sentences.zh: 坐軍敗，征還。

translations.literal: because of his defeat in battle, he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: but because of his defeat he was summoned back.

sentences.zh: 燕、秦相持經年，幽、冀大饑，人相食，邑落蕭條。

translations.literal: Yan and Qin faced one another for years; You and Ji suffered great famine, men ate one another, and settlements were desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Qin faced one another for years; You and Ji suffered great famine, people ate one another, and settlements lay desolate.

sentences.zh: 燕之軍士多餓死，燕王垂禁民養蠶，以桑椹為軍糧。

translations.literal: Many of Yan's soldiers starved to death; Yan King Murong Chui forbade the people to raise silkworms and used mulberries as army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Yan's soldiers starved to death; Yan king Murong Chui forbade the people to raise silkworms and used mulberries as army provisions.

sentences.zh: 垂將北趣中山，以驃騎大將軍農為前驅，前所假授吏眭邃等皆來迎候，上下如初，李乃服農之智略。

translations.literal: Chui was about to go north toward Zhongshan, with Flying Cavalry Grand General Nong as vanguard; the officials previously given provisional appointments, Sui Sui and the others, all came to welcome him, and superiors and subordinates were as before—only then did Li submit to Nong's wisdom and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Chui was about to march north toward Zhongshan with Flying Cavalry grand general Nong as vanguard. The officials he had given provisional appointments, Sui Sui and the others, all came to welcome him, and relations were as before—only then did Li acknowledge Nong's wisdom and strategy.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子好專權，復為奸諂者所構扇，與太保安有隙。

translations.literal: Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi was fond of monopolizing power and was again incited by sycophants, so that he and Grand Marshal Sima An had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi was fond of monopolizing power and was again stirred up by sycophants, so that he and Grand Marshal Sima An were at odds.

sentences.zh: 安欲避之，會秦王堅來求救，安乃請自將救之。

translations.literal: An wished to avoid him; it happened that King Fu Jian of Qin came seeking rescue, and An thereupon asked to lead the relief himself.
translations.idiomatic: An wished to avoid him; when King Fu Jian of Qin came seeking rescue, An asked to lead the relief expedition himself.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，出鎮廣陵之步丘，築壘曰新城而居之。

translations.literal: On renxu, he went out to garrison Buchiu in Guangling, built a stockade called Xincheng, and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu he went out to garrison Buchiu in Guangling, built a stockade called Xincheng, and dwelt there.

sentences.zh: 蜀郡太守任權攻拔成都，斬秦益州刺史李丕，復取益州。

translations.literal: Administrator of Shujun Ren Quan attacked and took Chengdu, beheaded Former Qin Inspector of Yizhou Li Pi, and recovered Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Shujun Ren Quan attacked and took Chengdu, beheaded Former Qin inspector of Yizhou Li Pi, and recovered Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 新平糧竭矢盡，外救不至。

translations.literal: Xinping's grain was exhausted and arrows spent; outside relief did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Xinping's grain was exhausted and its arrows spent, and outside relief did not arrive.

sentences.zh: 後秦王萇使人謂苟輔曰：「吾方以義取天下，豈仇忠臣邪！

translations.literal: Later Qin King Yao Chang sent someone to say to Gou Fu: "I am just now taking the empire by righteousness—how could I bear enmity toward loyal ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin king Yao Chang sent someone to tell Gou Fu, "I am taking the empire by righteousness—how could I bear enmity toward loyal ministers!

sentences.zh: 卿但帥城中之人還長安，吾正欲得此城耳。」

translations.literal: Sir, you need only lead the people of the city back to Chang'an; I want precisely this city."
translations.idiomatic: You need only lead the people of the city back to Chang'an; I want precisely this city."

sentences.zh: 輔以為然，帥民五千口出城。

translations.literal: Fu believed him and led five thousand mouths of the people out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Fu believed him and led five thousand people out of the city.

sentences.zh: 萇圍而坑之，男女無遺，獨馮傑子終得脫，奔長安。

translations.literal: Chang surrounded them and buried them alive; men and women, none were spared. Only Feng Jie's son Zhong escaped and fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chang surrounded them and buried them alive, sparing neither men nor women. Only Feng Jie's son Zhong escaped and fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅追贈輔等官爵，皆謚曰節愍侯；

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin posthumously granted Fu and the others offices and ranks, all with posthumous title Marquis of Jiemin;
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian posthumously granted Fu and the others offices and ranks, all with the posthumous title Marquis of Jiemin;

sentences.zh: 以終為新平太守。

translations.literal: he appointed Zhong Administrator of Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Zhong administrator of Xinping.

sentences.zh: 翟真自承營徙屯行唐，真司馬鮮于乞殺真及諸翟，自立為趙王。

translations.literal: Zhai Zhen moved his encampment from Chengying to Xingtang. Zhen's Major Xuanyu Qi killed Zhen and all the Zhai clan and declared himself King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Zhen moved his encampment from Chengying to Xingtang. Zhen's major Xuanyu Qi killed Zhen and all the Zhai clan and declared himself King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 營人共殺乞，立真從弟成為主；

translations.literal: The men of the camp jointly killed Qi and set up Zhen's younger cousin from the collateral line Cheng as leader;
translations.idiomatic: The men of the camp jointly killed Qi and set up Zhen's younger cousin Cheng as leader;

sentences.zh: 其眾多降於燕。

translations.literal: most of his followers surrendered to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: and most of his followers surrendered to Yan.

sentences.zh: 五月，西燕主沖攻長安，秦王堅身自督戰，飛矢滿體，流血淋漓。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Western Yan ruler Murong Chong attacked Chang'an. King Fu Jian of Qin personally supervised the battle; flying arrows covered his body and blood streamed down.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Western Yan ruler Murong Chong attacked Chang'an. King Fu Jian personally supervised the battle; flying arrows covered his body and blood streamed down.

sentences.zh: 沖縱兵暴掠，關中士民流散，道路斷絕，千里無煙。

translations.literal: Chong let his troops rampage and plunder; gentry and commoners of Guanzhong scattered, roads were cut off, and for a thousand li there was no smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Chong let his troops rampage and plunder; the gentry and commoners of Guanzhong scattered, roads were cut off, and for a thousand li there was no smoke of hearth fires.

sentences.zh: 有堡壁三十餘，推平遠將軍趙敖為主，相與結盟，冒難遣兵糧助堅，多為西燕兵所殺。

translations.literal: More than thirty stockades and walls chose Pingyuan General Zhao Ao as leader, formed alliances with one another, and braved hardship to send troops and grain to aid Fu Jian; many were killed by Western Yan troops.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty stockades chose Pingyuan general Zhao Ao as leader, formed alliances, and braved hardship to send troops and grain to aid Fu Jian, but many were killed by Western Yan troops.

sentences.zh: 堅謂之曰：「聞來者率不善達，此誠忠臣之義。

translations.literal: Fu Jian said to them: "I hear that those who come generally do not succeed in arriving—this is truly the duty of loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian told them, "I hear that those who come generally fail to arrive—this is truly the duty of loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 然今寇難殷繁，非一人之力所能濟也。

translations.literal: Yet now bandit calamities are pressing and numerous; this is not something one man's strength can remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now bandit calamities press on every side; this is not something one man's strength can remedy.

sentences.zh: 徒相隨入虎口，何益？

translations.literal: You would only follow one another into the tiger's maw—what good would it do?
translations.idiomatic: You would only follow one another into the tiger's maw—what good would that do?

sentences.zh: 汝曹宜為國自愛，畜糧厲兵，以俟天時，庶幾善不終否，有時而泰也！」

translations.literal: You ought to cherish yourselves for the state's sake, store grain and sharpen weapons, and await Heaven's season—perhaps good will not end in denial, and there will be a time of peace!"
translations.idiomatic: You ought to cherish yourselves for the state's sake, store grain and sharpen weapons, and await Heaven's season—perhaps good will not end in denial, and there will be a time of peace!"

sentences.zh: 三輔之民為沖所略者，遣人密告堅，請遣兵攻沖，欲縱火為內應。

translations.literal: People of the Three Adjuncts who had been plundered by Chong sent someone in secret to inform Fu Jian, asking him to send troops to attack Chong and intending to set fires as an inside response.
translations.idiomatic: People of the Three Adjuncts who had been plundered by Chong sent someone in secret to inform Fu Jian, asking him to send troops to attack Chong and intending to set fires as an inside response.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「甚哀諸卿忠誠！

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "I deeply pity your loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "I deeply pity your loyalty!

sentences.zh: 然吾猛士如虎豹，利兵如霜雪，困於烏合之虜，豈非天乎？

translations.literal: Yet my fierce warriors are like tigers and leopards, sharp weapons like frost and snow—yet we are trapped by a mob of rabble. Is this not Heaven's will?
translations.idiomatic: Yet my fierce warriors are like tigers and leopards, my sharp weapons like frost and snow—yet we are trapped by a mob of rabble. Is this not Heaven's will?

sentences.zh: 恐徒使諸卿坐自夷滅，吾不忍也！」

translations.literal: I fear I would only make you all sit and bring destruction on yourselves—I cannot bear it!"
translations.idiomatic: I fear I would only bring destruction on you all—I cannot bear it!"

sentences.zh: 其人固請不已，乃遣七百騎赴之。

translations.literal: The man pressed his request without cease, so he sent seven hundred horsemen to go.
translations.idiomatic: The man pressed his request without cease, so he sent seven hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 沖營縱火者，反為風火所燒，其得免者什一二；

translations.literal: Those who set fires in Chong's camp were instead burned by wind and fire; only one or two in ten escaped;
translations.idiomatic: Those who set fires in Chong's camp were instead burned by wind and fire; only one or two in ten escaped;

sentences.zh: 堅祭而哭之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian performed sacrifices and wept for them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian performed sacrifices and wept for them.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍楊定與沖戰於城西，為沖所擒。

translations.literal: Guard General Yang Ding fought Chong west of the city and was captured by Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Guard General Yang Ding fought Chong west of the city and was captured by Chong.

sentences.zh: 定，秦之驍將也。

translations.literal: Ding was a fierce general of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was one of Qin's fiercest generals.

sentences.zh: 堅大懼，以讖書云「帝出五將久長得」，乃留太子宏守長安，謂之曰：「天其或者欲導予出外。

translations.literal: Fu Jian was greatly afraid. Because a prophetic text said, "When the emperor goes out to the Five Generals, he will long obtain," he left Crown Prince Hong to hold Chang'an and said to him: "Perhaps Heaven wishes to guide me abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was greatly afraid. Because a prophetic text said, "When the emperor goes out to the Five Generals, he will long obtain," he left Crown Prince Hong to hold Chang'an and told him, "Perhaps Heaven wishes to guide me abroad.

sentences.zh: 汝善守城，勿與賊爭利，吾當出隴收兵運糧以給汝。」

translations.literal: You must hold the city well; do not contend for advantage with the bandits. I shall go out to Long and gather troops and transport grain to supply you."
translations.idiomatic: Hold the city well; do not contend for advantage with the bandits. I shall go out to Long and gather troops and transport grain to supply you."

sentences.zh: 遂帥騎數百與張夫人及中山公詵、二女寶、錦出奔五將山，宣告州郡，期以孟冬救長安。

translations.literal: He then led several hundred horsemen with Lady Zhang, Duke of Zhongshan Shen, and his two daughters Bao and Jin in flight to Mount Wujiang, proclaiming to the provinces and commanderies that he would rescue Chang'an by mid-winter.
translations.idiomatic: He then led several hundred horsemen with Lady Zhang, Duke of Zhongshan Shen, and his two daughters Bao and Jin in flight to Mount Wujiang, proclaiming to the provinces and commanderies that he would rescue Chang'an by mid-winter.

sentences.zh: 堅過襲韭園，李辯奔燕，彭和正慚，自殺。

translations.literal: As Fu Jian passed by to raid Jiuyuan, Li Bian fled to Yan and Peng Hezheng, in shame, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: As Fu Jian passed by to raid Jiuyuan, Li Bian fled to Yan and Peng Hezheng, in shame, killed himself.

sentences.zh: 閏月，以廣州刺史羅友為益州刺史，鎮成都。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Luo You, Inspector of Guangzhou, was appointed Inspector of Yizhou to garrison Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Luo You, inspector of Guangzhou, was appointed inspector of Yizhou to garrison Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，燕王垂至常山，圍翟成於行唐。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Yan King Murong Chui reached Changshan and besieged Zhai Cheng at Xingtang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Yan king Murong Chui reached Changshan and besieged Zhai Cheng at Xingtang.

sentences.zh: 命帶方王佐鎮龍城。

translations.literal: He ordered Prince of Daifang Zuo to garrison Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Prince of Daifang Zuo to garrison Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 六月，高句麗寇遼東，佐遣司馬郝景將兵救之，為高句麗所敗，高句麗遂陷遼東、玄菟。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Koguryŏ raided Liaodong. Zuo sent Major Hao Jing to lead troops to rescue it, but they were defeated by Koguryŏ, and Koguryŏ then took Liaodong and Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Koguryŏ raided Liaodong. Zuo sent Major Hao Jing to lead troops to the rescue, but they were defeated by Koguryŏ, which then took Liaodong and Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 秦太子宏不能守長安，將數千騎與母、妻、宗室西奔下辨；

translations.literal: Former Qin Crown Prince Hong could not hold Chang'an and led several thousand horsemen with his mother, wife, and members of the imperial clan in flight west to Xiabian;
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin crown prince Hong could not hold Chang'an and led several thousand horsemen with his mother, wife, and members of the imperial clan in flight west to Xiabian;

sentences.zh: 百官逃散，司隸校尉權翼等數百人奔後秦。

translations.literal: the hundred officials scattered in flight; Director of the Masters of Writing Quan Yi and several hundred others fled to Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: the hundred officials scattered in flight; Director of the Masters of Writing Quan Yi and several hundred others fled to Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 西燕主衝入據長安，縱兵大掠，死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: The Western Yan ruler Murong Chong entered and seized Chang'an, let his troops plunder on a great scale, and the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Western Yan ruler Murong Chong entered and seized Chang'an, let his troops plunder on a great scale, and the dead were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，旱，饑，井皆竭。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, there was drought and famine, and all wells dried up.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, drought and famine struck, and all wells dried up.

sentences.zh: 後秦王萇自故縣如新平。

translations.literal: Later Qin King Yao Chang went from Guxian toward Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin king Yao Chang went from Guxian toward Xinping.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅至五將山，後秦王萇遣驍騎將軍吳忠帥騎圍之。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin reached Mount Wujiang. Later Qin King Yao Chang sent Valiant Cavalry General Wu Zhong to lead horsemen and surround him.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian reached Mount Wujiang. Later Qin king Yao Chang sent Valiant Cavalry General Wu Zhong to lead horsemen and surround him.

sentences.zh: 秦兵皆散走，獨侍御十數人在側，堅神色自若，坐而待之，召宰人進食。

translations.literal: All the Qin soldiers scattered and fled; only a dozen or so attendants remained at his side. Fu Jian's expression was calm as he sat and waited, summoning the cook to bring food.
translations.idiomatic: All the Qin soldiers scattered and fled; only a dozen or so attendants remained at his side. Fu Jian's expression was calm as he sat and waited, summoning the cook to bring food.

sentences.zh: 俄而忠至，執之，送詣新平，幽於別室。

translations.literal: Before long Zhong arrived, seized him, and sent him to Xinping, where he was confined in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhong arrived, seized him, and sent him to Xinping, where he was confined in a separate room.

sentences.zh: 太子宏至下辨，南秦州刺史楊璧拒之。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Hong reached Xiabian; Inspector of Southern Qinzhou Yang Bi refused him entry.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Hong reached Xiabian, but Inspector of Southern Qinzhou Yang Bi refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 璧妻，堅之女順陽公主也，棄其夫從宏。

translations.literal: Bi's wife was Fu Jian's daughter, Princess Shunyang; she abandoned her husband and followed Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's wife was Fu Jian's daughter, Princess Shunyang; she abandoned her husband and followed Hong.

sentences.zh: 宏奔武都，投氐豪強熙，假道來奔，詔處之江州。

translations.literal: Hong fled to Wudu, threw himself on the Di chieftain Xi, borrowed a route to come in surrender, and an edict settled him at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong fled to Wudu, threw himself on the Di chieftain Xi, borrowed a route to surrender, and an edict settled him at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 長樂公丕帥眾三萬自枋頭將歸鄴城，龍驤將軍檀玄擊之，戰於谷口，玄兵敗，丕復入鄴城。

translations.literal: Prince of Changle Fu Pi led thirty thousand men from Fangtou intending to return to Ye city. Dragon-soaring General Tan Xuan attacked him; they fought at Gukou, Xuan's army was defeated, and Pi re-entered Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changle Fu Pi led thirty thousand men from Fangtou back toward Ye. Dragon-soaring General Tan Xuan attacked him; they fought at Gukou, Xuan's army was defeated, and Pi re-entered Ye.

sentences.zh: 燕建節將軍餘巖叛，自武邑北趣幽州。

translations.literal: Yan Establishing Authority General Yu Yan rebelled and marched north from Wuyi toward Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Establishing Authority general Yu Yan rebelled and marched north from Wuyi toward Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂馳使敕幽州將平規曰：「固守勿戰，俟吾破丁零自討之。」

translations.literal: Yan King Murong Chui sent a swift messenger ordering Youzhou General Ping Gui: "Hold firm and do not fight; wait until I have broken the Dingling, then I myself will punish him."
translations.idiomatic: Yan king Murong Chui sent a swift messenger ordering Youzhou general Ping Gui, "Hold firm and do not fight; wait until I have broken the Dingling, then I myself will punish him."

sentences.zh: 規出戰，為巖所敗。

translations.literal: Gui went out to battle and was defeated by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui went out to battle and was defeated by Yan.

sentences.zh: 巖入薊，掠千餘戶而去，遂據令支。

translations.literal: Yan entered Ji, plundered more than a thousand households, and departed; he then seized Lingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan entered Ji, plundered more than a thousand households, and departed; he then seized Lingzhi.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，翟成長史鮮于得斬成出降；

translations.literal: On guiyou, Zhai Cheng's Chief Clerk Xuanyu De beheaded Cheng and came out in surrender;
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Zhai Cheng's chief clerk Xuanyu De beheaded Cheng and came out in surrender;

sentences.zh: 垂屠行唐，盡坑成眾。

translations.literal: Chui slaughtered Xingtang and buried alive all of Cheng's followers.
translations.idiomatic: Chui slaughtered Xingtang and buried alive all of Cheng's followers.

sentences.zh: 太保安有疾，求還，詔許之；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Sima An was ill and asked to return; an edict permitted it;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Sima An was ill and asked to return; an edict permitted it;

sentences.zh: 八月；

translations.literal: in the eighth month;
translations.idiomatic: in the eighth month;

sentences.zh: 安至建康。

translations.literal: An reached Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: An reached Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 甲午，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiawu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，建昌文靖公謝安薨。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Duke of Jianchang, posthumous name Wenjing, Xie An died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Duke of Jianchang, posthumous name Wenjing, Xie An died.

sentences.zh: 詔加殊禮，如大司馬溫故事。

translations.literal: An edict added extraordinary rites, following the precedent of Grand Marshal Wen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added extraordinary rites, following the precedent of Grand Marshal Wen.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以司徒琅邪王道子領揚州刺史、錄尚書、都督中外諸軍事，以尚書令謝石為衛將軍。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Minister of Education Prince of Langye Sima Daozi was made concurrent Inspector of Yangzhou, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without; Minister of the Masters of Writing Xie Shi was made Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Minister of Education Prince of Langye Sima Daozi was made concurrent inspector of Yangzhou, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and commander-in-chief of all military affairs within and without; Minister of the Masters of Writing Xie Shi was made guard general.

sentences.zh: 後秦王萇使求傳國璽於秦王堅曰：「萇次應歷數，可以為惠。」

translations.literal: Later Qin King Yao Chang sent someone to request the Imperial Seal from King Fu Jian of Qin, saying: "Chang is next in the succession of the calendar's numbers—you may show favor thereby."
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin king Yao Chang sent someone to request the Imperial Seal from King Fu Jian, saying, "Chang is next in the succession of the calendar's numbers—you may show favor thereby."

sentences.zh: 堅瞋目叱之曰：「小羌敢逼天子，五胡次序，無汝羌名。

translations.literal: Fu Jian glared and shouted at him: "Little Qiang, you dare press the Son of Heaven! Among the Five Barbarians in order, there is no Qiang name for you.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian glared and shouted at him, "Little Qiang, you dare press the Son of Heaven! Among the Five Barbarians in order, there is no Qiang name for you.

sentences.zh: 璽已送晉，不可得也！」

translations.literal: The seal has already been sent to Jin—it cannot be obtained!"
translations.idiomatic: The seal has already been sent to Jin—it cannot be obtained!"

sentences.zh: 萇復遣右司馬尹緯說堅，求為禪代；

translations.literal: Chang again sent Right Major Yin Wei to persuade Fu Jian, asking for abdication in his favor;
translations.idiomatic: Chang again sent Right Major Yin Wei to persuade Fu Jian, asking for abdication in his favor;

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「禪代，聖賢之事。

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "Abdication in favor of another is the affair of sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "Abdication in favor of another is the affair of sages and worthies.

sentences.zh: 姚萇叛賊，何得為之！」

translations.literal: Yao Chang is a rebel bandit—how can he do it!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang is a rebel bandit—how can he do it!"

sentences.zh: 堅與緯語，問緯：「在朕朝何官？」

translations.literal: Fu Jian conversed with Wei and asked Wei: "What office did you hold in my court?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian conversed with Wei and asked him, "What office did you hold in my court?"

sentences.zh: 緯曰：「尚書令史」。

translations.literal: Wei said: "Clerk to the Minister Over the Masses."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Clerk to the Minister Over the Masses."

sentences.zh: 堅歎曰：「卿，王景略為儔，宰相才也，而朕不知卿，宜其亡也！」

translations.literal: Fu Jian sighed and said: "Sir, you are the equal of Wang Jinglue—a talent for chancellor—and I did not know you; no wonder I perished!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sighed and said, "Sir, you are the equal of Wang Jinglue—a talent for chancellor—and I did not know you; no wonder I perished!"

sentences.zh: 堅自以平生遇萇有恩，尤忿之，數罵萇求死，謂張夫人曰：「豈可令羌奴辱吾兒。」

translations.literal: Fu Jian, considering that in his lifetime he had shown Chang favor, was especially resentful; he repeatedly cursed Chang and sought death, and said to Lady Zhang: "How can I let the Qiang slave disgrace my sons."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian, considering that in his lifetime he had shown Chang favor, was especially resentful; he repeatedly cursed Chang and sought death, and told Lady Zhang, "How can I let the Qiang slave disgrace my sons."

sentences.zh: 乃先殺寶、錦。

translations.literal: He then killed Bao and Jin first.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed Bao and Jin first.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，萇遣人縊堅於新平佛寺，張夫人、中山公詵皆自殺，後秦將士皆為之哀慟。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Chang sent someone to strangle Fu Jian at the Buddhist temple in Xinping. Lady Zhang and Duke of Zhongshan Shen both killed themselves, and the officers and soldiers of Later Qin all mourned for them.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Chang sent someone to strangle Fu Jian at the Buddhist temple in Xinping. Lady Zhang and Duke of Zhongshan Shen both killed themselves, and the officers and soldiers of Later Qin all mourned for them.

sentences.zh: 萇欲隱其名，謚堅曰壯烈天王。

translations.literal: Chang wished to conceal his name and gave Fu Jian the posthumous title Martial and Fierce Heavenly King.
translations.idiomatic: Chang wished to conceal his name and gave Fu Jian the posthumous title Martial and Fierce Heavenly King.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：論者皆以為秦王堅之亡，由不殺慕容垂、姚萇故也，臣獨以為不然。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: Critics all hold that King Fu Jian of Qin's fall came from not killing Murong Chui and Yao Chang; your subject alone holds that this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Guang says: Critics all hold that King Fu Jian of Qin's fall came from not killing Murong Chui and Yao Chang; your subject alone holds that this is not so.

sentences.zh: 許劭謂魏武帝治世之能臣，亂世之奸雄。

translations.literal: Xu Shao said of Emperor Wu of Wei that in an age of order he would be a capable minister, but in an age of disorder a treacherous hero.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao said of Emperor Wu of Wei that in an age of order he would be a capable minister, but in an age of disorder a treacherous hero.

sentences.zh: 使堅治國無失其道，則垂、萇皆秦之能臣也，烏能為亂哉！

translations.literal: Had Fu Jian governed the state without losing the Way, then Chui and Chang would both have been capable ministers of Qin—how could they have made disorder!
translations.idiomatic: Had Fu Jian governed the state without losing the Way, then Chui and Chang would both have been capable ministers of Qin—how could they have made disorder!

sentences.zh: 堅之所以亡，由驟勝而驕故也。

translations.literal: The reason Fu Jian perished was that after sudden victories he grew arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: The reason Fu Jian perished was that after sudden victories he grew arrogant.

sentences.zh: 魏文侯問李克吳之所以亡，對曰：「數戰數勝。」

translations.literal: Marquis Wen of Wei asked Li Ke why Wu perished. He replied: "Repeated battles and repeated victories."
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Wen of Wei asked Li Ke why Wu perished. He replied, "Repeated battles and repeated victories."

sentences.zh: 文侯曰：「數戰數勝，國之福也，何故亡？」

translations.literal: The marquis said: "Repeated battles and repeated victories are a state's blessing—why then did it perish?"
translations.idiomatic: The marquis said, "Repeated battles and repeated victories are a state's blessing—why then did it perish?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「數戰則民疲，數勝則主驕，以驕主御疲民，未有不亡者也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "When battles are repeated the people grow weary; when victories are repeated the ruler grows arrogant. With an arrogant ruler commanding weary people, there has never been one who did not perish."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "When battles are repeated the people grow weary; when victories are repeated the ruler grows arrogant. With an arrogant ruler commanding weary people, there has never been one who did not perish."

sentences.zh: 秦王堅似之矣。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin resembled this.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin resembled this.

sentences.zh: 長樂公丕在鄴，將西赴長安，幽州刺史王永在壺關，遣使招丕，丕乃帥鄴中男女六萬餘口西如潞川，驃騎將軍張蚝、并州刺史王騰迎之入晉陽。

translations.literal: Prince of Changle Fu Pi was at Ye and was about to go west to Chang'an. Inspector of Youzhou Wang Yong was at Huguan and sent a messenger to summon Pi. Pi then led more than sixty thousand men and women of Ye west toward Luchuan; Flying Cavalry General Zhang Hao and Inspector of Bingzhou Wang Teng welcomed him into Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changle Fu Pi was at Ye and was about to go west to Chang'an. Inspector of Youzhou Wang Yong was at Huguan and sent a messenger to summon Pi. Pi then led more than sixty thousand men and women of Ye west toward Luchuan; Flying Cavalry general Zhang Hao and inspector of Bingzhou Wang Teng welcomed him into Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 王永留平州刺史苻沖守壺關，自帥騎一萬會丕於晉陽。

translations.literal: Wang Yong left Inspector of Pingzhou Fu Chong to hold Huguan and personally led ten thousand horsemen to join Pi at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong left Inspector of Pingzhou Fu Chong to hold Huguan and personally led ten thousand horsemen to join Pi at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 丕始知長安不守，堅已死，乃發喪，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Pi only then learned that Chang'an could not be held and that Fu Jian was already dead; he thereupon proclaimed mourning and declared himself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Pi only then learned that Chang'an could not be held and that Fu Jian was already dead; he thereupon proclaimed mourning and declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 追謚堅曰宣昭皇帝，廟號世祖，大赦，改元大安。

translations.literal: He gave Fu Jian the posthumous title Emperor Xuanzhao and temple name Shizu, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Fu Jian the posthumous title Emperor Xuanzhao and temple name Shizu, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Da'an.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂以魯王和為南中郎將，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: Yan ruler Murong Chui made Prince of Lu He Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Palace General and garrisoned him at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ruler Murong Chui made Prince of Lu He Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Palace general and garrisoned him at Ye.

sentences.zh: 遣慕容農出蠮螉塞，歷凡城，趣龍城，會兵討餘巖，慕容麟、慕容隆自信都徇勃海、清河。

translations.literal: He sent Murong Nong out through the Mantis Pass, passed through Fancheng, and hastened to Longcheng to gather troops to punish Yu Yan; Murong Lin and Murong Long marched from Xindu through Bohai and Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Murong Nong out through the Mantis Pass, passed through Fancheng, and hastened to Longcheng to gather troops to punish Yu Yan; Murong Lin and Murong Long marched from Xindu through Bohai and Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 麟擊勃海太守封懿，執之，因屯歷口。

translations.literal: Lin attacked Administrator of Bohai Feng Yi, seized him, and encamped at Likou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin attacked administrator of Bohai Feng Yi, seized him, and encamped at Likou.

sentences.zh: 懿，放之子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Feng Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was the son of Feng Fang.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑劉頭眷擊破賀蘭部於善無，又破柔然於意親山。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Liu Toujuan defeated the Helan tribe at Shanwu and again defeated the Rouran at Mount Yiqin.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei Liu Toujuan defeated the Helan tribe at Shanwu and again defeated the Rouran at Mount Yiqin.

sentences.zh: 頭眷子羅辰言於頭眷曰：「比來行兵，所向無敵。

translations.literal: Toujuan's son Luochen said to Toujuan: "Of late in campaigning, wherever we go we are without rival.
translations.idiomatic: Toujuan's son Luochen said to Toujuan, "Of late in campaigning, wherever we go we are without rival.

sentences.zh: 然心腹之疾，願早圖之！」

translations.literal: Yet there is a malady of the heart and belly—I wish you would plan against it early!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet there is a malady of the heart and belly—I wish you would plan against it early!"

sentences.zh: 頭眷曰：「誰也？」

translations.literal: Toujuan said: "Who is it?"
translations.idiomatic: Toujuan said, "Who is it?"

sentences.zh: 羅辰曰：「從兄顯，忍人也，必將為亂。」

translations.literal: Luochen said: "Your cousin Xian is a cruel man and will surely make disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Luochen said, "Your cousin Xian is a cruel man and will surely make disorder."

sentences.zh: 頭眷不聽。

translations.literal: Toujuan did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Toujuan did not listen.

sentences.zh: 顯，庫仁之子也。

translations.literal: Xian was the son of Kuren.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was the son of Kuren.

sentences.zh: 頃之，顯果殺頭眷自立。

translations.literal: Before long, Xian indeed killed Toujuan and declared himself ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Xian indeed killed Toujuan and declared himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 又將殺拓跋珪，顯弟亢泥妻，珪之姑也，以告珪母賀氏。

translations.literal: He was also about to kill Tuoba Gui. Xian's younger brother Kangni's wife was Gui's paternal aunt; she informed Gui's mother, Lady He.
translations.idiomatic: He was also about to kill Tuoba Gui. Xian's younger brother Kangni's wife was Gui's paternal aunt; she informed Gui's mother, Lady He.

sentences.zh: 顯謀主梁六眷，代王什翼犍之甥也，亦使其部人穆崇、奚牧密告珪，且以其愛妻、駿馬付崇曰：「事洩，當以此自明。」

translations.literal: Xian's chief plotter Liang Liuquan was a nephew of Dai King Shiyijian and also had his tribesmen Mu Chong and Xi Mu secretly inform Gui, giving Chong his beloved wife and thoroughbred horses and saying: "If the affair is exposed, use these to prove yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Xian's chief plotter Liang Liuquan was a nephew of Dai king Shiyijian and also had his tribesmen Mu Chong and Xi Mu secretly inform Gui, giving Chong his beloved wife and thoroughbred horses and saying, "If the affair is exposed, use these to prove yourself."

sentences.zh: 賀氏夜飲顯酒，令醉，使珪陰與舊臣長孫犍、元他、羅結輕騎亡去。

translations.literal: Lady He by night gave Xian wine to drink and made him drunk, then had Gui secretly with old ministers Changsun Jian, Yuan Tuo, and Luo Jie flee away on light horses.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He by night gave Xian wine to drink and made him drunk, then had Gui secretly flee with old ministers Changsun Jian, Yuan Tuo, and Luo Jie on light horses.

sentences.zh: 向晨，賀氏故驚廄中群馬，使顯起視之。

translations.literal: Toward dawn, Lady He deliberately startled the herd of horses in the stable, making Xian rise to look.
translations.idiomatic: Toward dawn, Lady He deliberately startled the herd of horses in the stable, making Xian rise to look.

sentences.zh: 賀氏哭曰：「吾子適在此，今皆不見，汝等誰殺之邪？」

translations.literal: Lady He cried and said: "My son was just here, and now none of them can be seen—who among you killed him?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady He cried and said, "My son was just here, and now none of them can be seen—who among you killed him?"

sentences.zh: 顯以故不急追。

translations.literal: For this reason Xian did not pursue in haste.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Xian did not pursue in haste.

sentences.zh: 珪遂奔賀蘭部，依其舅賀訥，訥驚喜曰：「復國之後，當念老臣！」

translations.literal: Gui thereupon fled to the Helan tribe and relied on his maternal uncle He Ne. Ne said in alarm and delight: "When you restore the state, you must remember this old minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Gui thereupon fled to the Helan tribe and relied on his maternal uncle He Ne. Ne said in alarm and delight, "When you restore the state, you must remember this old minister!"

sentences.zh: 珪笑曰：「誠如舅言，不敢忘也。」

translations.literal: Gui smiled and said: "If it is truly as my uncle says, I dare not forget."
translations.idiomatic: Gui smiled and said, "If it is truly as my uncle says, I dare not forget."

sentences.zh: 顯疑梁六眷洩其謀，將囚之。

translations.literal: Xian suspected that Liang Liuquan had leaked his plot and was about to imprison him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian suspected that Liang Liuquan had leaked his plot and was about to imprison him.

sentences.zh: 穆崇宣言曰：「六眷不顧恩義，助顯為逆，我掠得其妻馬，足以解忿。」

translations.literal: Mu Chong proclaimed publicly: "Liujuan showed no regard for kindness and righteousness and helped Xian in rebellion; I plundered his wife and horses, which is enough to vent my anger."
translations.idiomatic: Mu Chong proclaimed publicly, "Liujuan showed no regard for kindness and righteousness and helped Xian in rebellion; I plundered his wife and horses, which is enough to vent my anger."

sentences.zh: 顯乃捨之。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon released him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian thereupon released him.

sentences.zh: 賀氏從弟外朝大人賀悅舉所部以奉珪。

translations.literal: Lady He's younger cousin from her mother's clan, Outer Court Great Man He Yue, raised his following to serve Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He's younger cousin from her mother's clan, Outer Court Great Man He Yue, raised his following to serve Gui.

sentences.zh: 顯怒，將殺賀氏，賀氏奔亢泥家，匿神車中三日，亢泥舉家為之請，乃得免。

translations.literal: Xian was enraged and was about to kill Lady He. Lady He fled to Kangni's house and hid in the divine chariot for three days; Kangni's entire household pleaded on her behalf, and she was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was enraged and was about to kill Lady He. Lady He fled to Kangni's house and hid in the sacred chariot for three days; Kangni's entire household pleaded on her behalf, and she was spared.

sentences.zh: 故南部大人長孫嵩帥所部七百餘家叛顯，將奔五原。

translations.literal: Former Southern Great Man Changsun Song led more than seven hundred households of his following in rebellion against Xian and was about to flee to Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Former Southern Great Man Changsun Song led more than seven hundred households of his following in rebellion against Xian and was about to flee to Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 時拓跋寔君之子渥亦聚眾自立，嵩欲歸之；

translations.literal: At that time Tuoba Shijun's son Wo also gathered a host and declared himself ruler, and Song wished to join him;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tuoba Shijun's son Wo also gathered a host and declared himself ruler, and Song wished to join him;

sentences.zh: 烏渥謂嵩曰：「逆父之子，不足從也。

translations.literal: Wu Wo said to Song: "The son of a father-killer is not worth following.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wo said to Song, "The son of a father-killer is not worth following.

sentences.zh: 不如歸珪。」

translations.literal: Better to join Gui."
translations.idiomatic: Better to join Gui."

sentences.zh: 嵩從之。

translations.literal: Song followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Song followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 久之，劉顯所部有亂，故中部大人庾和辰奉賀氏奔珪。

translations.literal: After some time, disorder broke out among Liu Xian's following, and former Central Great Man Yu Hechen escorted Lady He in flight to Gui.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, disorder broke out among Liu Xian's following, and former Central Great Man Yu Hechen escorted Lady He in flight to Gui.

sentences.zh: 賀訥弟染干以珪得眾心，忌之，使其黨侯引七突殺珪；

translations.literal: He Ne's younger brother Rangan, jealous because Gui had won the hearts of the people, had his partisan Houyin Qitu kill Gui;
translations.idiomatic: He Ne's younger brother Rangan, jealous because Gui had won the hearts of the people, had his partisan Houyin Qitu kill Gui;

sentences.zh: 代人尉古真知之，以告珪，侯引七突不敢發。

translations.literal: the native of Dai, Weiguzhen, learned of it and informed Gui, and Houyin Qitu did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: the native of Dai, Weiguzhen, learned of it and informed Gui, and Houyin Qitu did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 染干疑古真洩其謀，執而訊之，以兩車軸夾其頭，傷一目，不伏，乃免之。

translations.literal: Rangan suspected that Weiguzhen had leaked his plot; he seized and interrogated him, clamping his head between two cart axles and injuring one eye. Weiguzhen did not confess, and Rangan then released him.
translations.idiomatic: Rangan suspected that Weiguzhen had leaked his plot; he seized and interrogated him, clamping his head between two cart axles and injuring one eye. Weiguzhen did not confess, and Rangan then released him.

sentences.zh: 染干遂舉兵圍珪；

translations.literal: Rangan thereupon raised troops and besieged Gui;
translations.idiomatic: Rangan thereupon raised troops and besieged Gui;

sentences.zh: 賀氏出謂染干曰：「汝等欲於何置我，而殺吾子乎！」

translations.literal: Lady He came out and said to Rangan: "Where do you intend to place me, yet kill my son!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady He came out and said to Rangan, "Where do you intend to place me, yet kill my son!"

sentences.zh: 染干慚而去。

translations.literal: Rangan withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Rangan withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 九月，秦主丕以張蚝為侍中、司空，王永為侍中、都督中外諸軍事、車騎大將軍、尚書令，王騰為中軍大將軍、司隸校尉，苻沖為尚書左僕射，封西平王；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, King Fu Pi of Qin appointed Zhang Hao as Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, Wang Yong as Palace Attendant, Director General of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Director of the Masters of Writing, Wang Teng as Grand General of the Central Army and Director of Retainers, and Fu Chong as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffing him as King of Xiping;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, King Fu Pi of Qin appointed Zhang Hao Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, Wang Yong Palace Attendant, Director General of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Director of the Masters of Writing, Wang Teng Grand General of the Central Army and Director of Retainers, and Fu Chong Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffing him as King of Xiping;

sentences.zh: 又以左長史楊輔為右僕射，右長史王亮為護軍將軍；

translations.literal: he further appointed Left Chief Clerk Yang Fu as Right Vice Director and Right Chief Clerk Wang Liang as General Who Guards the Army;
translations.idiomatic: he further appointed Left Chief Clerk Yang Fu Right Vice Director and Right Chief Clerk Wang Liang General Who Guards the Army;

sentences.zh: 立妃楊氏為皇后，子寧為皇太子，壽為長樂王，鏘為平原王，懿為勃海王，昶為濟北王。

translations.literal: he established Consort Yang as empress, his son Ning as crown prince, Shou as King of Changle, Qiang as King of Pingyuan, Yi as King of Bohai, and Chang as King of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: he established Consort Yang as empress, his son Ning as crown prince, Shou as King of Changle, Qiang as King of Pingyuan, Yi as King of Bohai, and Chang as King of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 呂光自龜茲還至宜禾，秦涼州刺史梁熙謀閉境拒之。

translations.literal: Lü Guang returned from Kucha to Yiho, and Former Qin Inspector of Liangzhou Liang Xi planned to close the borders and keep him out.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang returned from Kucha to Yiho, and Former Qin Inspector of Liangzhou Liang Xi planned to close the borders and keep him out.

sentences.zh: 高昌太守楊翰言於熙曰：「呂光新破西域，兵強氣銳，聞中原喪亂，必有異圖。

translations.literal: Administrator of Gaochang Yang Han said to Xi: "Lü Guang has newly conquered the Western Regions; his troops are strong and his spirit keen. Hearing of disorder in the Central Plains, he is sure to harbor other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Gaochang Yang Han said to Xi, "Lü Guang has newly conquered the Western Regions; his troops are strong and his spirit keen. Hearing of disorder in the Central Plains, he is sure to harbor other designs.

sentences.zh: 河西地方萬里，帶甲十萬，足以自保。

translations.literal: The Hexi region spans ten thousand li and can field a hundred thousand armored men—enough to defend itself.
translations.idiomatic: The Hexi region spans ten thousand li and can field a hundred thousand armored men—enough to defend itself.

sentences.zh: 若光出流沙，其勢難敵。

translations.literal: If Guang emerges from the shifting sands, his force will be hard to withstand.
translations.idiomatic: If Guang emerges from the shifting sands, his force will be hard to withstand.

sentences.zh: 高梧谷口險阻之要，宜先守之而奪其水；

translations.literal: The mouth of Gaowu Valley is a strategic choke point; you should hold it first and cut off their water;
translations.idiomatic: The mouth of Gaowu Valley is a strategic choke point; you should hold it first and cut off their water;

sentences.zh: 波既窮渴，可以坐制。

translations.literal: once they are exhausted by thirst, you can control them without moving.
translations.idiomatic: once they are exhausted by thirst, you can control them without moving.

sentences.zh: 如以為遠，伊吾關亦可拒也。

translations.literal: If you think that too distant, Yiwu Pass can also be used to block them.
translations.idiomatic: If you think that too distant, Yiwu Pass can also be used to block them.

sentences.zh: 度此二□厄，雖有子房之策，無所施矣！」

translations.literal: Once they pass these two narrow passes, even Zhang Liang's stratagems would have nowhere to be applied!"
translations.idiomatic: Once they pass these two narrow passes, even Zhang Liang's stratagems would have nowhere to be applied!"

sentences.zh: 熙弗聽。

translations.literal: Xi did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xi did not listen.

sentences.zh: 美水令犍為張統謂熙曰：「今關中大亂，京師存亡不可知。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Meishui, the native of Jianwei Zhang Tong, said to Xi: "Now Guanzhong is in great disorder, and whether the capital survives is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Meishui, the native of Jianwei Zhang Tong, said to Xi, "Now Guanzhong is in great disorder, and whether the capital survives is unknown.

sentences.zh: 呂光之來，其志難測，將軍何以拒之？」

translations.literal: When Lü Guang comes, his intent will be hard to fathom—how will the general resist him?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Guang comes, his intent will be hard to fathom—how will the general resist him?"

sentences.zh: 熙曰：「憂之，未知所出。」

translations.literal: Xi said: "I am worried, but do not know what course to take."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "I am worried, but do not know what course to take."

sentences.zh: 統曰：「光智略過人，今擁思歸之士，乘戰勝之氣，其鋒未易當也。

translations.literal: Tong said: "Guang's wisdom and strategy surpass other men. He now commands troops longing to return home and rides the momentum of victory—his edge is not easily matched.
translations.idiomatic: Tong said, "Guang's wisdom and strategy surpass other men. He now commands troops longing to return home and rides the momentum of victory—his edge is not easily matched.

sentences.zh: 將軍世受大恩，忠誠夙著；

translations.literal: The general has for generations received great favor, and your loyalty has long been manifest;
translations.idiomatic: The general has for generations received great favor, and your loyalty has long been manifest;

sentences.zh: 立勳王室，宜在今日！

translations.literal: to establish merit for the royal house—today is the day!
translations.idiomatic: to establish merit for the royal house—today is the day!

sentences.zh: 行唐公洛，上之從弟，勇冠一時，為將軍計，莫若奉為盟主以收眾望，推忠義以帥群豪，則光雖至，不敢有異心也。

translations.literal: Duke of Xingtang Luo is the sovereign's younger cousin; his courage stands foremost in the age. For the general's plan, none is better than to install him as covenant leader to win popular esteem and lead the heroes by righteousness—then even if Guang arrives, he will not dare harbor other thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Xingtang Luo is the sovereign's younger cousin; his courage stands foremost in the age. For the general's plan, none is better than to install him as covenant leader to win popular esteem and lead the heroes by righteousness—then even if Guang arrives, he will not dare harbor other thoughts.

sentences.zh: 資其精銳，東兼毛興，連王統、楊璧，合四州之眾，掃凶逆，寧王室，此桓、文之舉也。」

translations.literal: With his elite forces, join Mao Xing in the east, link with Wang Tong and Yang Bi, unite the hosts of four provinces, sweep away the wicked and rebels, and settle the royal house—this would be an act worthy of Duke Huan and Duke Wen."
translations.idiomatic: With his elite forces, join Mao Xing in the east, link with Wang Tong and Yang Bi, unite the hosts of four provinces, sweep away the wicked and rebels, and settle the royal house—this would be an act worthy of Duke Huan and Duke Wen."

sentences.zh: 熙又弗聽，殺洛於西海。

translations.literal: Xi again did not listen and killed Luo at Xihai.
translations.idiomatic: Xi again did not listen and killed Luo at Xihai.

sentences.zh: 光聞楊翰之謀，懼，不敢進。

translations.literal: Guang heard of Yang Han's plan, grew afraid, and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Guang heard of Yang Han's plan, grew afraid, and did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 杜進曰：「梁熙文雅有餘，機鑒不足，終不能用翰之謀，不足憂也。

translations.literal: Du Jin said: "Liang Xi has more than enough refinement and polish, but not enough insight and discernment; in the end he will not adopt Han's plan—there is nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jin said, "Liang Xi has more than enough refinement and polish, but not enough insight and discernment; in the end he will not adopt Han's plan—there is nothing to worry about.

sentences.zh: 宜及其上下離心，速進以取之。」

translations.literal: We should strike while his superiors and subordinates are divided in heart and advance quickly to take him."
translations.idiomatic: We should strike while his superiors and subordinates are divided in heart and advance quickly to take him."

sentences.zh: 光從之。

translations.literal: Guang followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Guang followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 進至高昌，楊翰以郡迎降。

translations.literal: Advancing to Gaochang, Yang Han surrendered the commandery in welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Gaochang, Yang Han surrendered the commandery in welcome.

sentences.zh: 至玉門，熙移檄責光擅命還師，以子胤為鷹揚將軍，與振威將軍南安姚皓、別駕衛翰帥眾五萬拒光於酒泉。

translations.literal: Reaching Yumen, Xi issued a proclamation rebuking Guang for returning on his own authority without orders; he made his son Yin General of the Soaring Hawk, and together with General Who Shakes Might Yao Hao of Nan'an and Chief Clerk Wei Han led fifty thousand men to resist Guang at Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Yumen, Xi issued a proclamation rebuking Guang for returning on his own authority without orders; he made his son Yin General of the Soaring Hawk, and together with General Who Shakes Might Yao Hao of Nan'an and Chief Clerk Wei Han led fifty thousand men to resist Guang at Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 敦煌太守姚靜、晉昌太守李純以郡降光。

translations.literal: Administrator of Dunhuang Yao Jing and Administrator of Jinchang Li Chun surrendered their commanderies to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Dunhuang Yao Jing and Administrator of Jinchang Li Chun surrendered their commanderies to Guang.

sentences.zh: 光報檄涼州，責熙無赴難之志，五遏歸國之眾；

translations.literal: Guang replied with a proclamation to Liangzhou, rebuking Xi for lacking the will to rush to the realm's aid and for five times blocking the troops returning home;
translations.idiomatic: Guang replied with a proclamation to Liangzhou, rebuking Xi for lacking the will to rush to the realm's aid and for five times blocking the troops returning home;

sentences.zh: 遣彭晁、杜進、姜飛為前鋒，與胤戰於安彌，大破擒之。

translations.literal: he sent Peng Chao, Du Jin, and Jiang Fei as vanguard, fought Yin at Anmi, inflicted a great defeat, and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Peng Chao, Du Jin, and Jiang Fei as vanguard, fought Yin at Anmi, routed him, and captured him.

sentences.zh: 於是四山胡、夷皆附於光。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Hu and Yi of the four mountains all submitted to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Hu and Yi of the four mountains all submitted to Guang.

sentences.zh: 武威太守彭濟執熙以降，光殺之。

translations.literal: Administrator of Wuwei Peng Ji seized Xi and surrendered; Guang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Wuwei Peng Ji seized Xi and surrendered; Guang killed him.

sentences.zh: 光入姑臧，自領涼州刺史，表杜進為武威太守，自餘將佐，各受職位。

translations.literal: Guang entered Guzang, personally assumed the post of Inspector of Liangzhou, memorialized Du Jin as Administrator of Wuwei, and had all remaining officers and aides receive their appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Guang entered Guzang, personally assumed the post of Inspector of Liangzhou, memorialized Du Jin as Administrator of Wuwei, and had all remaining officers and aides receive their appointments.

sentences.zh: 涼州郡縣皆降於光，獨酒泉太守宋皓、西郡太守索泮城守不下。

translations.literal: The commanderies and counties of Liangzhou all surrendered to Guang; only Administrator of Jiuquan Song Hao and Administrator of Xijun Suo Pan held their cities and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The commanderies and counties of Liangzhou all surrendered to Guang; only Administrator of Jiuquan Song Hao and Administrator of Xijun Suo Pan held their cities and would not submit.

sentences.zh: 光攻而執之，讓泮曰：「吾受詔平西域，而梁熙絕我歸路，此朝廷之罪人，卿何為附之？」
