translations.literal: Guang attacked and captured them, and rebuked Pan, saying: "I received orders to pacify the Western Regions, yet Liang Xi cut off my road home—he is a criminal of the court. Why do you attach yourself to him?"
translations.idiomatic: Guang attacked and captured them, and rebuked Pan, saying, "I received orders to pacify the Western Regions, yet Liang Xi cut off my road home—he is a criminal of the court. Why do you attach yourself to him?"

sentences.zh: 泮曰：「將軍受詔平西域，不受詔亂涼州，梁公何罪而將軍殺之？

translations.literal: Pan said: "The general received orders to pacify the Western Regions, not orders to throw Liangzhou into disorder—what crime did Duke Liang commit that the general killed him?
translations.idiomatic: Pan said, "The general received orders to pacify the Western Regions, not orders to throw Liangzhou into disorder—what crime did Duke Liang commit that the general killed him?

sentences.zh: 泮但苦力不足，不能報君父之仇耳，豈肯如逆氐彭濟之所為乎！

translations.literal: Pan only grieves that his strength is insufficient and he cannot avenge his lord and father—how could he be willing to act like the rebellious Di Peng Ji!
translations.idiomatic: Pan only grieves that his strength is insufficient and he cannot avenge his lord and father—how could he be willing to act like the rebellious Di Peng Ji!

sentences.zh: 主滅臣死，固其常也。」

translations.literal: When the lord perishes the minister dies—such is the constant way."
translations.idiomatic: When the lord perishes the minister dies—such is the constant way."

sentences.zh: 光殺泮及皓。

translations.literal: Guang killed Pan and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Guang killed Pan and Hao.

sentences.zh: 主簿尉祐，奸佞傾險，與彭濟同執熙，光寵信之。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Wei You was treacherous, fawning, and dangerously cunning; he had joined Peng Ji in seizing Xi, and Guang favored and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Wei You was treacherous, fawning, and dangerously cunning; he had joined Peng Ji in seizing Xi, and Guang favored and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 祐譖殺名士姚皓等十餘人，涼州人由是不悅。

translations.literal: You slandered and had more than ten eminent men, including Yao Hao, killed, and the people of Liangzhou were thereby displeased.
translations.idiomatic: You slandered and had more than ten eminent men, including Yao Hao, killed, and the people of Liangzhou were thereby displeased.

sentences.zh: 光以祐為金城太守，祐至允吾，襲據其城以叛；

translations.literal: Guang appointed You Administrator of Jincheng; when You reached Yunwu, he seized the city by surprise and rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: Guang appointed You Administrator of Jincheng; when You reached Yunwu, he seized the city by surprise and rebelled;

sentences.zh: 姜飛擊破之，祐奔據興城。

translations.literal: Jiang Fei defeated him, and You fled to hold Xingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Fei defeated him, and You fled to hold Xingcheng.

sentences.zh: 乞伏國仁自稱大都督、大將軍、單于，領秦、河二州牧，改元建義，以乙旃童泥為左相，屋引出支為右相，獨孤匹蹄為左輔，武群勇士為右輔，弟乾歸為上將軍，分其地置武城等十二郡，築勇士城而都之。

translations.literal: Qifu Guoren declared himself Grand Governor, Grand General, and Chanyu, and assumed the posts of regional inspector of Qin and He provinces; he changed the era name to Jianyi, appointed Yizhan Tongni as Left Chancellor, Wuyin Chuzhi as Right Chancellor, Dugu Piti as Left Assistant, Wuqun Yongshi as Right Assistant, and his younger brother Qian'gui as Upper General; he divided his territory and established twelve commanderies including Wucheng, built Yongshi City, and made it his capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Guoren declared himself Grand Governor, Grand General, and Chanyu, and assumed the posts of regional inspector of Qin and He provinces; he changed the era name to Jianyi, appointed Yizhan Tongni Left Chancellor, Wuyin Chuzhi Right Chancellor, Dugu Piti Left Assistant, Wuqun Yongshi Right Assistant, and his younger brother Qian'gui Upper General; he divided his territory and established twelve commanderies including Wucheng, built Yongshi City, and made it his capital.

sentences.zh: 秦尚書令魏昌公纂自關中奔晉陽；

translations.literal: Former Qin Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Weichang Fu Zuan, fled from Guanzhong to Jinyang;
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Weichang Fu Zuan, fled from Guanzhong to Jinyang;

sentences.zh: 秦主丕拜纂太尉，封東海王。

translations.literal: King Fu Pi of Qin appointed Zuan Grand Commandant and enfeoffed him as King of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Pi appointed Zuan Grand Commandant and enfeoffed him as King of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，西燕主沖遣尚書令高蓋帥眾五萬伐後秦，戰於新平南，蓋大敗，降於後秦。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Western Yan ruler Murong Chong sent Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Gai to lead fifty thousand men against Later Qin; they fought south of Xinping, Gai suffered a great defeat, and surrendered to Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Western Yan ruler Murong Chong sent Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Gai to lead fifty thousand men against Later Qin; they fought south of Xinping, Gai suffered a great defeat, and surrendered to Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 初，蓋以楊定為子，及蓋敗，定亡奔隴右，復收集其舊眾。

translations.literal: Earlier Gai had taken Yang Ding as his adopted son; when Gai was defeated, Ding fled to Longyou and again gathered his former following.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gai had taken Yang Ding as his adopted son; when Gai was defeated, Ding fled to Longyou and again gathered his former following.

sentences.zh: 苻定、苻紹、苻謨、苻亮聞秦主丕即位，皆自河北遣使謝罪。

translations.literal: Fu Ding, Fu Shao, Fu Mo, and Fu Liang, hearing that King Fu Pi of Qin had acceded to the throne, all sent envoys from Hebei to submit apologies.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ding, Fu Shao, Fu Mo, and Fu Liang, hearing that King Fu Pi of Qin had acceded to the throne, all sent envoys from Hebei to submit apologies.

sentences.zh: 中山太守王兗，本新平氐也，固守博陵，為秦拒燕。

translations.literal: Administrator of Zhongshan Wang Yan, originally a Di of Xinping, held firm at Boling and resisted Yan on Qin's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Zhongshan Wang Yan, originally a Di of Xinping, held firm at Boling and resisted Yan on Qin's behalf.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丕以兗為平州刺史，定為冀州牧，紹為冀州都督，謨為幽州牧，亮為幽、平二州都督，並進郡公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Pi appointed Yan Inspector of Pingzhou, Ding regional inspector of Jizhou, Shao Director of Jizhou, Mo regional inspector of Youzhou, and Liang Director of You and Ping provinces, all promoted to full dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Pi appointed Yan Inspector of Pingzhou, Ding regional inspector of Jizhou, Shao Director of Jizhou, Mo regional inspector of Youzhou, and Liang Director of You and Ping provinces, all promoted to full dukes.

sentences.zh: 左將軍竇沖據茲川，有眾數萬，與秦州刺史王統、河州刺史毛興、益州刺史王廣、南秦州刺史楊璧、衛將軍楊定皆自隴右遣使邀丕，共擊後秦。

translations.literal: Left General Dou Chong held Zichuan with a host of tens of thousands; together with Inspector of Qinzhou Wang Tong, Inspector of Hezhou Mao Xing, Inspector of Yizhou Wang Guang, Inspector of South Qinzhou Yang Bi, and Guard General Yang Ding, he all sent envoys from Longyou inviting Pi to join in attacking Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Left General Dou Chong held Zichuan with a host of tens of thousands; together with Inspector of Qinzhou Wang Tong, Inspector of Hezhou Mao Xing, Inspector of Yizhou Wang Guang, Inspector of South Qinzhou Yang Bi, and Guard General Yang Ding, he all sent envoys from Longyou inviting Pi to join in attacking Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 丕以定為雍州牧，沖為梁州牧，加統鎮西大將軍，興車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Pi made Ding regional inspector of Yongzhou and Chong regional inspector of Liangzhou, added to Tong the title Grand General Who Guards the West, and to Xing the title Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Pi made Ding regional inspector of Yongzhou and Chong regional inspector of Liangzhou, added to Tong the title Grand General Who Guards the West, and to Xing the title Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 璧征南大將軍，並開府儀同三司，加廣安西將軍，皆進位州牧。

translations.literal: Bi was made Grand General Who Conquers the South, and all were granted offices with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies; Guang was added as Grand General Who Pacifies the West, and all were promoted to regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was made Grand General Who Conquers the South, and all were granted offices with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies; Guang was added as Grand General Who Pacifies the West, and all were promoted to regional inspector.

sentences.zh: 楊定尋徙治歷城，置儲蓄於百頃，自稱龍驤將軍、仇池公，遣使來稱籓；

translations.literal: Yang Ding soon moved his seat of government to Licheng, established stores at Baikeng, styled himself General of the Soaring Dragon and Duke of Chouci, and sent envoys to submit as a vassal state;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ding soon moved his seat of government to Licheng, established stores at Baikeng, styled himself General of the Soaring Dragon and Duke of Chouci, and sent envoys to submit as a vassal state;

sentences.zh: 詔因其所號假之。

translations.literal: an edict granted him those titles he had claimed.
translations.idiomatic: an edict granted him those titles he had claimed.

sentences.zh: 其後又取天水、略陽之地，自稱秦州刺史、隴西王。

translations.literal: Afterward he also took the lands of Tianshui and Lueyang and styled himself Inspector of Qinzhou and King of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he also took the lands of Tianshui and Lueyang and styled himself Inspector of Qinzhou and King of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 繹幕人蔡匡據城以叛燕，燕慕容麟、慕容隆共攻之。

translations.literal: Cai Kuang of Yimu seized the city and rebelled against Yan; Murong Lin and Murong Long of Yan jointly attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Kuang of Yimu seized the city and rebelled against Yan; Murong Lin and Murong Long of Yan jointly attacked him.

sentences.zh: 泰山太守任泰潛師救匡，至匡壘南八里，燕人乃覺之。

translations.literal: Administrator of Taishan Ren Tai secretly led troops to rescue Kuang; when they reached eight li south of Kuang's fort, the Yan forces only then detected them.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Taishan Ren Tai secretly led troops to rescue Kuang; when they reached eight li south of Kuang's fort, the Yan forces only then detected them.

sentences.zh: 諸將以匡未下而外敵奄至，甚患之。

translations.literal: The generals, because Kuang had not yet submitted while outside enemies suddenly arrived, were greatly troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The generals, because Kuang had not yet submitted while outside enemies suddenly arrived, were greatly troubled.

sentences.zh: 隆曰：「匡恃外救，故不時下。

translations.literal: Long said: "Kuang relies on outside relief, and so will not submit promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Long said, "Kuang relies on outside relief, and so will not submit promptly.

sentences.zh: 今計泰之兵不過數千人，及其未合，擊之，泰敗，匡自降矣。」

translations.literal: Now I estimate Tai's troops are no more than a few thousand; before they join forces, strike them—when Tai is defeated, Kuang will submit of himself."
translations.idiomatic: Now I estimate Tai's troops are no more than a few thousand; before they join forces, strike them—when Tai is defeated, Kuang will submit of himself."

sentences.zh: 乃釋匡擊泰，大破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: They thereupon left Kuang aside and struck Tai, inflicting a great defeat and beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon left Kuang aside and struck Tai, inflicting a great defeat and beheading more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 匡遂降，燕王垂殺之，且屠其壘。

translations.literal: Kuang thereupon submitted; Yan King Murong Chui killed him and moreover slaughtered his fort.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang thereupon submitted; Yan king Murong Chui killed him and moreover slaughtered his fort.

sentences.zh: 慕容農至龍城，休士馬十餘日。

translations.literal: Murong Nong reached Longcheng and rested troops and horses for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong reached Longcheng and rested troops and horses for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「殿下之來，取道甚速，今至此。

translations.literal: The generals all said: "When Your Highness came, you took the road with great speed and have now reached here.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all said, "When Your Highness came, you took the road with great speed and have now reached here.

sentences.zh: 久留不進，何也？」

translations.literal: You linger long without advancing—why?"
translations.idiomatic: You linger long without advancing—why?"

sentences.zh: 農曰：「吾來速者，恐餘巖過山鈔盜，侵擾良民耳。

translations.literal: Nong said: "I came swiftly because I feared Yu Yan would cross the mountains to plunder and rob, harassing the good people.
translations.idiomatic: Nong said, "I came swiftly because I feared Yu Yan would cross the mountains to plunder and rob, harassing the good people.

sentences.zh: 巖才不逾人，誑誘饑兒，烏集為群，非有綱紀。

translations.literal: Yan's talent does not surpass other men's; he deceives and lures hungry youths, who gather like crows in flocks—there is no discipline among them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's talent does not surpass other men's; he deceives and lures hungry youths, who gather like crows in flocks—there is no discipline among them.

sentences.zh: 吾已扼其喉，久將離散，無能為也。

translations.literal: I have already seized him by the throat; in time they will scatter and can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: I have already seized him by the throat; in time they will scatter and can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 今此田善熟，未收而行，徒自耗損；

translations.literal: Now the fields here are ripening well; to march before the harvest would only waste our own strength;
translations.idiomatic: Now the fields here are ripening well; to march before the harvest would only waste our own strength;

sentences.zh: 當俟收畢，往則梟之，亦不出旬日耳。」

translations.literal: we should wait until the harvest is complete; when we go we will behead him—it will not exceed ten days."
translations.idiomatic: we should wait until the harvest is complete; when we go we will behead him—it will not exceed ten days."

sentences.zh: 頃之，農將步騎三萬至令支，巖眾震駭，稍稍逾城歸農。

translations.literal: Before long, Nong led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to Lingzhi; Yan's followers were shaken in terror and gradually crossed the walls to return to Nong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Nong led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to Lingzhi; Yan's followers were shaken in terror and gradually crossed the walls to return to Nong.

sentences.zh: 巖計窮出降，農斬之。

translations.literal: Yan, his stratagems exhausted, came out and submitted; Nong beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, his stratagems exhausted, came out and submitted; Nong beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 進擊高句麗，復遼東、玄菟二郡。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Goguryeo, he recovered the two commanderies of Liaodong and Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to attack Goguryeo, he recovered the two commanderies of Liaodong and Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 還至龍城上，上疏請繕修陵廟。

translations.literal: Returning to Longcheng, he submitted a memorial requesting repairs to the tombs and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Longcheng, he submitted a memorial requesting repairs to the tombs and temples.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂以農為使持節、都督幽、平二州、北狄諸軍事、幽州牧，鎮龍城。

translations.literal: Yan King Murong Chui appointed Nong bearer of credentials, Director of You and Ping provinces and of all military affairs of the Northern Di, and regional inspector of Youzhou, to garrison Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan king Murong Chui appointed Nong bearer of credentials, Director of You and Ping provinces and of all military affairs of the Northern Di, and regional inspector of Youzhou, to garrison Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 徙平州刺史帶方王佐鎮平郭。

translations.literal: He moved Inspector of Pingzhou Prince of Daifang Zuo to garrison Pingguo.
translations.idiomatic: He moved Inspector of Pingzhou Prince of Daifang Zuo to garrison Pingguo.

sentences.zh: 農於是創立法制，事從寬簡，清刑獄，省賦役，勸課農桑，居民富贍，四方流民前後至者數萬口。

translations.literal: Nong thereupon established laws and institutions, keeping affairs lenient and simple, clearing the prisons, reducing taxes and corvée, encouraging agriculture and sericulture; the residents grew rich and provided for, and wandering people from all directions came in succession by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Nong thereupon established laws and institutions, keeping affairs lenient and simple, clearing the prisons, reducing taxes and corvée, and encouraging agriculture and sericulture; the residents grew rich and provided for, and wandering people from all directions came in succession by tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 先是幽、冀流民多入高句麗，農以驃騎司馬范陽龐淵為遼東太守，招撫之。

translations.literal: Before this, wandering people of You and Ji for the most part entered Goguryeo; Nong made Pang Yuan of Fanyang, cavalry commandant, Administrator of Liaodong to summon and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, many refugees from You and Ji had fled into Goguryeo. Nong appointed Pang Yuan of Fanyang, cavalry commandant, as Administrator of Liaodong to recall and settle them.

sentences.zh: 慕容麟攻王兗於博陵，城中糧竭矢盡，功曹張猗逾城出，聚眾以應麟。

translations.literal: Murong Lin attacked Wang Yan at Boling; within the city grain was exhausted and arrows spent. Registrar Zhang Yi went over the wall, gathered a crowd, and responded to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin besieged Wang Yan at Boling. When the city ran out of grain and arrows, Registrar Zhang Yi slipped over the wall, raised a band of men, and joined Lin.

sentences.zh: 兗臨城數之曰：「卿是秦民，吾是卿君，卿起兵應賊，自號『義兵』，何名實之相違也？

translations.literal: Yan faced the city and rebuked him, saying: "You are a subject of Qin; I am your lord. You raised troops to respond to the enemy and styled yourself 'Righteous Army'—how do name and fact contradict one another?
translations.idiomatic: Yan stood before the walls and rebuked him: "You are a man of Qin and I am your lord. You took up arms for the enemy and call yourself the 'Righteous Army'—how can the name and the deed so utterly disagree?

sentences.zh: 古人求忠臣必於孝子之門，卿母在城，棄而不顧，吾何有焉！

translations.literal: The ancients sought loyal ministers only at the doors of filial sons. Your mother is in the city, yet you abandoned her without regard—what do I find in you!
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that loyal ministers are found only in the houses of filial sons. Your mother is still in this city, yet you cast her aside—what worth do I see in you at all!

sentences.zh: 今人取卿一切之功則可矣，寧能忘卿不忠不孝之事乎！

translations.literal: If men today take all your achievements, so be it—but can they forget your acts of disloyalty and unfiliality!
translations.idiomatic: Let the world take whatever credit you have earned—but can it ever forget your treachery and your betrayal of your mother!

sentences.zh: 不意中州禮義之邦，乃有如卿者也！」

translations.literal: I never expected that the Central Land, realm of ritual and righteousness, would produce one such as you!"
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that the heartland of ritual and righteousness could breed a man like you!"

sentences.zh: 十二月，麟拔博陵，執兗及苻鑒，殺之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Lin captured Boling, seized Yan and Fu Jian, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Lin took Boling, captured Yan and Fu Jian, and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 昌黎太守宋敞帥烏桓、索頭之眾救兗，不及而還。

translations.literal: Administrator of Changli Song Chang led Wuhuan and Suotou forces to rescue Yan but arrived too late and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Song Chang, Administrator of Changli, marched with Wuhuan and Suotou troops to relieve Yan, but arrived too late and turned back.

sentences.zh: 秦主丕以敞為平州刺史。

translations.literal: King Fu Pi of Qin made Chang Regional Inspector of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Pi of Qin appointed Song Chang Regional Inspector of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂北如中山，謂諸將曰：「樂浪王招流散，實倉廩，外給軍糧，內營宮室，雖蕭何何以加之！」

translations.literal: Yan King Murong Chui went north to Zhongshan and said to his generals: "The Prince of Lelang gathers the scattered, fills the granaries, supplies army grain from without and builds palaces within—even Xiao He could not surpass him!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan King Murong Chui traveled north to Zhongshan and told his generals, "The Prince of Lelang has recalled the displaced, filled the storehouses, fed the armies abroad and raised palaces at home—even Xiao He himself could hardly have done more!"

sentences.zh: 丙申，垂始定都中山。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Chui first established his capital at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Chui fixed his capital at Zhongshan for the first time.

sentences.zh: 秦苻定據信都以拒燕，燕王垂以從弟北地王精為冀州刺史，將兵攻之。

translations.literal: Fu Ding of Qin held Xindu to resist Yan; Yan King Chui made his younger cousin Prince of Beidi Jing regional inspector of Jizhou and led troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ding of Qin held Xindu against the Yan advance. Yan King Chui appointed his cousin Prince of Beidi Jing regional inspector of Jizhou and marched to attack him.

sentences.zh: 拓跋珪從曾祖紇羅與其弟建及諸部大人，共請賀訥推珪為主。

translations.literal: Tuoba Gui's granduncle Heluo, together with his younger brother Jian and the chiefs of the various tribes, jointly requested He Ne to install Gui as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui's granduncle Heluo, his younger brother Jian, and the chiefs of the tribes together asked He Ne to raise Gui as their leader.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝中之上太元十一年（

translations.literal: From the middle section of Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong line, Taixuan year 11 (
translations.idiomatic: From the middle portion of Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong line, Taixuan year 11 (

sentences.zh: 丙戌，公元三八六年）

translations.literal: bingxu, CE 386)
translations.idiomatic: bingxu, CE 386)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊申，拓跋珪大會於牛川，即代王位，改元登國。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on wushen, Tuoba Gui held a great assembly at Niuchuan, assumed the title King of Dai, and changed the era name to Dengguo.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on wushen, Tuoba Gui convened a great assembly at Niuchuan, took the throne as King of Dai, and proclaimed the era name Dengguo.

sentences.zh: 以長孫嵩為南部大人，叔孫普洛為北部大人，分治其眾。

translations.literal: He appointed Changsun Song southern chief and Shusun Pulo northern chief to govern the people in division.
translations.idiomatic: He made Changsun Song chief of the south and Shusun Pulo chief of the north, dividing the people between them.

sentences.zh: 以上谷張兗為左長史，許謙為右司馬，廣寧王建、代人和跋、叔孫建、庾岳等為外朝大人，奚牧為治民長，皆掌宿衛及參軍國謀議。

translations.literal: He made Zhang Yan of Shanggu left chief secretary, Xu Qian right marshal, Wang Jian of Guangning, He Ba of Dai, Shusun Jian, Yu Yue, and others outer-court chiefs, and Xi Mu chief who governs the people—all charged with palace guard and participation in state counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan of Shanggu became left chief secretary and Xu Qian right marshal; Wang Jian of Guangning, He Ba of Dai, Shusun Jian, Yu Yue, and others were made chiefs of the outer court; Xi Mu was made chief administrator of the people. All were charged with guarding the ruler and advising on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 長孫道生、賀毘等侍從左右，出納教命。

translations.literal: Changsun Daisheng, He Pi, and others attended at his left and right, receiving and issuing commands.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Daisheng, He Pi, and others waited at his side, bearing his orders in and out.

sentences.zh: 王建娶代王什翼犍之女；

translations.literal: Wang Jian married the daughter of King Shiyijian of Dai;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian had married a daughter of King Shiyijian of Dai;

sentences.zh: 岳，和辰之弟；

translations.literal: Yue was the younger brother of Hechen;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue was Hechen's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 道生，嵩之從子也。

translations.literal: Daisheng was Song's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Daisheng was Changsun Song's nephew.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Yan King Chui assumed the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: Yan King Murong Chui declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 後秦王萇如安定。

translations.literal: Later Qin King Chang went to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin King Fu Chang traveled to Anding.

sentences.zh: 南安秘宜帥羌、胡五萬餘人攻乞伏國仁，國仁將兵五千逆擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Mi Yi of Nan'an led more than fifty thousand Qiang and Hu to attack Qifu Guoren; Guoren led five thousand troops to meet and strike them and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Yi of Nan'an marched more than fifty thousand Qiang and Hu against Qifu Guoren. Guoren met him with five thousand men and routed the host.

sentences.zh: 宜奔還南安。

translations.literal: Yi fled back to Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Yi fled back to Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 鮮于乞之殺翟真也，翟遼奔黎陽，黎陽太守滕恬之甚愛信之。

translations.literal: When Xianyu Qi killed Zhai Zhen, Zhai Liao fled to Liyang; Administrator of Liyang Teng Tianzhi deeply favored and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianyu Qi killed Zhai Zhen, Zhai Liao fled to Liyang, where Administrator Teng Tianzhi came to favor and trust him deeply.

sentences.zh: 恬之喜畋獵，不愛士卒，遼潛施奸惠以收從心。

translations.literal: Tianzhi loved hunting and did not care for the soldiers; Liao secretly dispensed covert kindness to win their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhi loved the chase and neglected his troops; Liao quietly bought their loyalty with secret favors.

sentences.zh: 恬之南攻鹿鳴城，遼於後閉門拒之；

translations.literal: When Tianzhi marched south to attack Luming city, Liao closed the gates behind him and barred him;
translations.idiomatic: When Tianzhi marched south to attack Luming, Liao shut the gates behind him and refused him entry;

sentences.zh: 恬之東奔鄄城，遼追執之，遂據黎陽。

translations.literal: Tianzhi fled east to Juancheng; Liao pursued, seized him, and then held Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhi fled east toward Juancheng; Liao overtook and captured him, then seized Liyang for himself.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史朱序遣將軍秦膺、童斌與淮、泗諸郡共討之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yuzhou Zhu Xu sent Generals Qin Ying and Tong Bin together with the commanderies of Huai and Si to attack him jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu, Inspector of Yuzhou, sent Generals Qin Ying and Tong Bin, together with the Huai and Si commanderies, to join in suppressing him.

sentences.zh: 秦益州牧王廣自隴右引兵攻河州牧毛興於枹罕，興遣建節將軍衛平帥其宗人一千七百夜襲廣，大破之。

translations.literal: Wang Guang, regional inspector of Yizhou of Qin, led troops from Longyou to attack Mao Xing, regional inspector of Hezhou, at Fuhan; Xing sent General Who Establishes Authority Wei Ping to lead seventeen hundred of his clansmen in a night raid on Guang and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guang, Qin regional inspector of Yizhou, marched from Longyou to attack Mao Xing, regional inspector of Hezhou, at Fuhan. Xing sent General Wei Ping with seventeen hundred clansmen on a night raid and shattered Guang's army.

sentences.zh: 二月，秦州牧王統遣兵助廣攻興，興嬰城自守。

translations.literal: In the second month, Wang Tong, regional inspector of Qinzhou, sent troops to aid Guang in attacking Xing; Xing defended the city with what he had.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Wang Tong, regional inspector of Qinzhou, sent reinforcements to help Guang against Xing. Xing tied himself to the walls and held on.

sentences.zh: 燕大赦，改元建興，置公卿尚書百官，繕宗廟、社稷。

translations.literal: Yan proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Jianxing, established the ranks of dukes, ministers, and secretaries with the full bureaucracy, and repaired the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yan declared a general amnesty, changed the era name to Jianxing, set up the full court from dukes and ministers to secretaries, and restored the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 西燕主沖樂在長安，且畏燕主垂強，不敢東歸，課農築室，為久安之計，鮮卑鹹怨之。

translations.literal: Western Yan ruler Chong delighted in Chang'an and feared Yan King Chui's strength, daring not return east; he assigned the farmers to build dwellings for a long-term settling plan, and the Xianbei all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Western Yan ruler Murong Chong had grown fond of Chang'an and feared Murong Chui's power, so he dared not return east. He set the farmers to building houses as though settling for good, and the Xianbei resented him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 左將軍韓延因眾心不悅，攻沖，殺之，立衝將段隨為燕王，改元昌平。

translations.literal: Left General Han Yan, because the people's hearts were discontent, attacked Chong, killed him, and installed Chong's general Duan Sui as Yan King, changing the era name to Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Left General Han Yan, finding the army restive, rose against Chong, killed him, and set Chong's general Duan Sui on the throne as Yan King, proclaiming the era name Changping.

sentences.zh: 初，張天錫之南奔也，秦長水校尉王穆匿其世子大豫，與俱奔河西，依禿髮思復鞬，思復鞬送於魏安。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zhang Tianxi fled south, Wang Mu, colonel of changshui of Qin, hid his heir Da Yu and fled west of the River with him to rely on Tufa Sifu; Sifu sent them on to Wei'an.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Tianxi fled south, Wang Mu, Qin's colonel of changshui, concealed his heir Zhang Da Yu and fled with him west of the River to seek refuge with Tufa Sifu, who sent them on to Wei'an.

sentences.zh: 魏安人焦松、齊肅、張濟等聚兵數千人迎大豫為主，攻呂光昌松郡，拔之，執太守王世強。

translations.literal: The men of Wei'an Jiao Song, Qi Su, Zhang Ji, and others gathered an army of several thousand to welcome Da Yu as leader, attacked Changsong commandery of Lü Guang, captured it, and seized Administrator Wang Shiqiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Song, Qi Su, Zhang Ji, and others of Wei'an raised several thousand men to welcome Da Yu as their leader. They attacked Lü Guang's Changsong commandery, took it, and captured its administrator Wang Shiqiang.

sentences.zh: 光使輔國將軍杜進擊之，進兵敗，大進豫逼姑臧。

translations.literal: Guang sent Assistant General Du Jin to attack them; Jin's army was defeated, and Da Yu pressed on toward Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Guang sent Assistant General Du Jin against them, but Jin was defeated and Da Yu advanced on Guzang.

sentences.zh: 王穆諫曰：「光糧豐城固，甲兵精銳，逼之非利；

translations.literal: Wang Mu remonstrated, saying: "Guang's grain is plentiful and his city strong, his armor and troops sharp and keen—to press him is not advantageous;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mu urged caution: "Guang's granaries are full and his walls strong, his arms and men first-rate. To press him now would bring no gain;

sentences.zh: 不如席捲嶺西，礪兵積粟，然後東向與之爭，不及期年，光可取也。」

translations.literal: better to sweep through west of the ranges, sharpen weapons and accumulate grain, then turn east to contend with him—in less than a full year, Guang can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: better to sweep through the lands west of the ranges, drill the troops and hoard grain, then turn east to fight him. In less than a year Guang can be taken."

sentences.zh: 大豫不從，自號撫軍將軍、涼州牧，改元鳳凰，以王穆為長史，傳檄郡縣，傳穆說諭嶺西諸郡，建康太守李隰、祁連都尉嚴純皆起兵應之，有眾三萬，保據楊塢。

translations.literal: Da Yu did not follow him. He styled himself General Who Pacifies the Army and regional inspector of Liangzhou, changed the era name to Fenghuang, made Wang Mu chief administrator, issued proclamations to the commanderies and counties, and sent Mu to persuade and instruct the western commanderies west of the ranges; Administrator of Jiankang Li Yin and Commandant of Qilianshan Yan Chun both raised troops in response, with a host of thirty thousand, holding Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Da Yu refused. He styled himself General Who Pacifies the Army and regional inspector of Liangzhou, proclaimed the era Fenghuang, and made Wang Mu his chief administrator. He issued proclamations throughout the commanderies and sent Mu to win over the western districts beyond the ranges. Li Yin, Administrator of Jiankang, and Yan Chun, Commandant of Qilian, both rose in support. With thirty thousand men they held Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 代王珪徙居定襄之盛樂，務農息民，國人悅之。

translations.literal: King Gui of Dai moved to Shengle in Dingxiang, devoted himself to farming and giving the people rest, and the people of the state were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: King Tuoba Gui moved his seat to Shengle in Dingxiang, devoted himself to agriculture and easing the people's burdens, and the realm rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 三月，大赦。

translations.literal: In the third month, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 泰山太守張願以郡叛，降翟遼。

translations.literal: Administrator of Taishan Zhang Yuan rebelled with the commandery and submitted to Zhai Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuan, Administrator of Taishan, rebelled with his commandery and surrendered to Zhai Liao.

sentences.zh: 初，謝玄欲使朱序屯梁國，玄自屯彭城，以北固河上，西援洛陽。

translations.literal: Initially, Xie Xuan wished to have Zhu Xu garrison Liangguo while he himself garrisoned Pengcheng, to secure the north on the Yellow River and aid Luoyang to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xie Xuan had planned to station Zhu Xu at Liangguo while he himself held Pengcheng, securing the north along the Yellow River and supporting Luoyang to the west.

sentences.zh: 朝議以征役既久，欲令玄置戍而還。

translations.literal: The court deliberated that because corvée and campaigns had been long, they wished to have Xuan establish garrisons and return.
translations.idiomatic: The court argued that the campaigns had dragged on too long and wanted Xuan to leave garrisons in place and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 會翟遼、張願繼叛，北方騷動，玄謝罪，乞解職，詔慰諭，令還淮陰。

translations.literal: When Zhai Liao and Zhang Yuan rebelled in succession and the north was in turmoil, Xuan submitted an apology and begged to be relieved of office; an edict comforted and instructed him, ordering him to return to Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Zhai Liao and Zhang Yuan rebelled in turn, throwing the north into unrest. Xuan submitted his resignation in apology; the throne reassured him by edict and ordered him back to Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂追尊母蘭氏為文昭皇后，欲遷文明段后，以蘭后配享太祖，詔百官議之，皆以為當然。

translations.literal: Yan King Chui posthumously honored his mother Lady Lan as Empress Wen Zhao and wished to move Empress Wenming of the Duan clan so that Lady Lan would share sacrifice with the Founding Emperor; he ordered the hundred officials to deliberate, and all held it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yan King Chui posthumously honored his mother Lady Lan as Empress Wen Zhao and proposed moving Empress Wenming of the Duan clan so that Lady Lan might share sacrifice with the Founding Emperor. He ordered the officials to debate the matter, and all agreed it was only right.

sentences.zh: 博士劉詳、董謐以為：「堯母為帝嚳妃，位第三，不以貴陵姜原。

translations.literal: Academicians Liu Xiang and Dong Mi held: "Emperor Yao's mother was a consort of Emperor Ku, ranked third—she did not, by virtue of rank, displace Jiang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians Liu Xiang and Dong Mi argued: "Emperor Yao's mother was a consort of Emperor Ku, ranked third among his wives; her eminence did not displace Jiang Yuan.

sentences.zh: 明聖之道，以至公為先；

translations.literal: The way of the wise and sage takes utmost fairness first;
translations.idiomatic: The way of the enlightened sage puts utmost fairness first;

sentences.zh: 文昭後宜立別廟。」

translations.literal: Empress Wen Zhao should have a separate temple established."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wen Zhao ought to receive a temple of her own."

sentences.zh: 垂怒，逼之，詳、謐曰：「上所欲為，無問於臣。

translations.literal: Chui was angry and pressed them; Xiang and Mi said: "What Your Majesty wishes to do needs no inquiry of us.
translations.idiomatic: Chui flew into a rage and pressed them. Xiang and Mi replied, "If Your Majesty has already decided, there is no need to ask us.

sentences.zh: 臣案經奉禮，不敢有貳。」

translations.literal: We examine the classics and uphold ritual—we dare not be of two minds."
translations.idiomatic: We serve the classics and uphold ritual, and we dare not speak with two tongues."

sentences.zh: 垂乃不復問諸儒，卒遷段后，以蘭后代之。

translations.literal: Chui then questioned the scholars no further; in the end he moved Empress Duan and had Lady Lan take her place.
translations.idiomatic: Chui questioned the scholars no more. In the end he moved Empress Duan aside and installed Lady Lan in her stead.

sentences.zh: 又以景昭可足渾后傾覆社稷，追廢之；

translations.literal: Also, because Empress Kehun of Jingzhao had overturned the altars of state, he posthumously deposed her;
translations.idiomatic: He also held that Empress Kehun of Jingzhao had brought the realm to ruin and posthumously stripped her of rank;

sentences.zh: 尊烈祖昭儀段氏為景德皇后，配享列祖。

translations.literal: he honored Liezong's consort Duan as Empress Jingde to share sacrifice with the successive ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: he honored Liezong's consort Lady Duan as Empress Jingde, granting her place beside the ancestral line.

sentences.zh: 崔鴻曰：「齊桓公命諸侯無發妾為妻。

translations.literal: Cui Hong said: "Duke Huan of Qi commanded the feudal lords: let no man take a concubine as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong wrote: "Duke Huan of Qi once commanded the feudal lords that no man should elevate a concubine to wife.

sentences.zh: 夫之於妻，猶不可以妾代之，況子而易其母乎？

translations.literal: Between husband and wife, a wife may not be replaced by a concubine—how much less may a son replace his mother!
translations.idiomatic: Even between husband and wife a concubine may not supplant the wife—how much less may a son displace his own mother!

sentences.zh: 《春秋》所稱母以子貴者，君母既沒，得以妾母為小君也；

translations.literal: What the Spring and Autumn Annals call 'the mother honored through the son' means: once the lord's proper mother is gone, a concubine mother may serve as lesser lady;
translations.idiomatic: When the Spring and Autumn speaks of 'a mother honored through her son,' it means that after the ruler's proper mother has died, a concubine who bore the heir may serve as lesser lady;

sentences.zh: 至於享祀宗廟，則成風終不得配莊公也。

translations.literal: yet when it comes to receiving sacrifice in the ancestral temple, Lady Cheng finally could not share sacrifice with Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: yet in sacrifice at the ancestral temple Lady Cheng was never permitted to share the altar with Duke Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 君父之所為，臣子必習而效之，猶形聲之於影響也。

translations.literal: What the lord and father do, ministers and sons must necessarily learn and imitate—as form and sound to shadow and echo.
translations.idiomatic: What rulers and fathers do, ministers and sons inevitably learn and copy, as the shadow and echo follow form and sound.

sentences.zh: 寶之逼殺其母，由垂為之漸也。

translations.literal: Bao's forcing and killing his mother stemmed from Chui's paving the way.
translations.idiomatic: That Murong Bao later drove his mother to her death began with the precedent Chui set.

sentences.zh: 堯、舜之讓，猶為之、噲之禍，況違禮而縱私者乎？

translations.literal: Even the abdications of Yao and Shun still brought the disaster of Zhi and Kuai—how much more those who violate ritual and indulge private feeling!
translations.idiomatic: Even the abdications of Yao and Shun led to the calamities of Zhi and Kuai—how much worse when ritual is cast aside for private ends!

sentences.zh: 昔文姜得罪於桓公，《春秋》不之廢。

translations.literal: Formerly Wen Jiang offended Duke Huan, yet the Spring and Autumn did not depose her for it.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Wen Jiang gave offense to Duke Huan, yet the Spring and Autumn Annals did not record her deposition.

sentences.zh: 可足渾氏雖有罪於前朝，然小君之禮成矣；

translations.literal: Although Lady Kehun had sinned against the former dynasty, the rites of a lesser lady were complete;
translations.idiomatic: Though Lady Kehun had sinned against the former court, the rites due a lesser lady had already been fulfilled;

sentences.zh: 垂以私憾廢之，又立兄妾之無子者，皆非禮也。

translations.literal: Chui deposed her from private resentment and also installed a lord's brother's concubine who had no son—both are unritual.
translations.idiomatic: Chui deposed her from private spite and elevated a childless concubine of his elder brother—both acts violated ritual.

sentences.zh: 劉顯自善無南走馬邑，其族人奴真帥所部降於代。

translations.literal: Liu Xian fled south from Shannwu to Mayi; his clansman Nuzhen led his division and submitted to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian fled south from Shannwu to Mayi. His kinsman Nuzhen brought his following over to Dai.

sentences.zh: 奴真有兄犍，先居賀蘭部，奴真言於代王珪，請召犍而以所部讓之；

translations.literal: Nuzhen had an elder brother Jian who had earlier lived in the Helan tribe; Nuzhen spoke to King Gui of Dai, requesting that Jian be summoned and the division given to him;
translations.idiomatic: Nuzhen had an elder brother Jian who had long lived among the Helan tribe. Nuzhen asked King Gui to summon Jian and yield his command to him;

sentences.zh: 珪許之。

translations.literal: Gui granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Gui agreed.

sentences.zh: 犍既領部，遣弟去斤遺賀訥金馬。

translations.literal: Once Jian took charge of the tribe, he sent his younger brother Qujin to present gold and horses to He Ne.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian took command of the tribe, he sent his younger brother Qujin to He Ne with gifts of gold and horses.

sentences.zh: 賀染干謂去斤曰：「待汝兄弟厚，汝今領部，宜來從我。」

translations.literal: He Rangan said to Qujin: "Your brothers have been treated generously. Now that you lead the tribe, you ought to come follow me."
translations.idiomatic: He Rangan told Qujin, "Your brothers have been treated well. Now that you command the tribe, you should come over to my side."

sentences.zh: 去斤許之。

translations.literal: Qujin agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Qujin consented.

sentences.zh: 奴真怒曰：「我祖父以來，世為代忠臣，故我以部讓汝等，欲為義也。

translations.literal: Nuzhen angrily said: "Since my grandfather's time our house has been loyal ministers of Dai generation after generation; therefore I gave the tribe to you, intending righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Nuzhen raged: "Since my grandfather's day our house has served Dai in loyalty, generation after generation. I yielded the tribe to you out of duty and honor.

sentences.zh: 今汝等無狀，乃謀叛國，義於何在！」

translations.literal: Now you are shameless and plot to rebel against the state—where is righteousness!"
translations.idiomatic: And now you disgrace yourselves by plotting rebellion—where is your honor!"

sentences.zh: 遂殺犍及去斤。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed Jian and Qujin.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed Jian and Qujin.

sentences.zh: 染干聞之，引兵攻奴真，奴真奔代。

translations.literal: Rangan heard of it and led troops to attack Nuzhen; Nuzhen fled to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When Rangan heard of it he marched against Nuzhen, who fled to Dai for refuge.

sentences.zh: 珪遣使責染干，染干乃止。

translations.literal: Gui sent an envoy to rebuke Rangan, and Rangan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gui sent envoys to rebuke Rangan, and Rangan desisted.

sentences.zh: 西燕左僕射慕容恆、尚書慕容永襲段隨，殺之；

translations.literal: Western Yan Left Vice Director Murong Heng and Secretary Murong Yong attacked Duan Sui and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Heng, Western Yan's Left Vice Director, and Secretary Murong Yong attacked Duan Sui and killed him;

sentences.zh: 立宜都王子顗為燕王，改元建明，帥鮮卑男女四十餘萬口去長安而東。

translations.literal: They installed Yidu Prince Yan's son Yan as Yan King, changed the era name to Jianming, and led more than four hundred thousand Xianbei men and women east from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: They set Yidu Prince Yan's son Yan on the throne as Yan King, proclaimed the era Jianming, and led more than four hundred thousand Xianbei men, women, and children eastward out of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 恆弟護軍將軍韜，誘顗於臨晉，恆怒，捨韜去詠與武衛將軍刁雲帥眾攻韜。

translations.literal: Heng's younger brother Protector General Han Yao lured Yan at Linjin; Heng was angry, abandoned Han Yao, and joined Murong Yong and Martial Guard General Diao Yun to lead troops against Han Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's younger brother Protector General Han Yao lured Prince Yan into a trap at Linjin. Heng, enraged, abandoned Han Yao and joined Murong Yong and Martial Guard General Diao Yun to attack him.

sentences.zh: 韜敗，奔恆營。

translations.literal: Han Yao was defeated and fled to Heng's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yao was beaten and fled back to Heng's camp.

sentences.zh: 恆立西燕主沖之子瑤為帝，改元建平，謚沖曰威皇帝。

translations.literal: Heng installed Western Yan ruler Chong's son Yao as emperor, changed the era name to Jianping, and gave Chong the posthumous title Emperor Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Heng enthroned Western Yan ruler Chong's son Yao as emperor, proclaimed the era Jianping, and posthumously titled Chong Emperor Wei.

sentences.zh: 眾皆去瑤奔永，永執瑤，殺之，立慕容泓子忠為帝，改元建武。

translations.literal: The masses all abandoned Yao and fled to Yong; Yong seized Yao, killed him, and installed Murong Hong's son Zhong as emperor, changing the era name to Jianwu.
translations.idiomatic: The people deserted Yao and rallied to Yong. Yong seized Yao, killed him, and raised Murong Hong's son Zhong as emperor under the era name Jianwu.

sentences.zh: 忠以永為太尉，守尚書令，封河東公。

translations.literal: Zhong made Yong Grand Commandant, acting Head of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong made Yong Grand Commandant and acting Head of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 永持法寬平，鮮卑安之。

translations.literal: Yong maintained the law with leniency and fairness, and the Xianbei were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yong enforced the law with leniency and evenhandedness, and the Xianbei were reassured.

sentences.zh: 至聞喜，聞燕主垂已稱尊號，不敢進，築燕熙城而居之。

translations.literal: Reaching Wenxi, they heard Yan King Chui had already assumed the honored title and dared not advance; they built Fortress Yanxi and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: At Wenxi they learned that Murong Chui had already taken the imperial title and dared not press eastward. They built Fortress Yanxi and settled there.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑既東，長安空虛。

translations.literal: Once the Xianbei had gone east, Chang'an was empty.
translations.idiomatic: With the Xianbei gone east, Chang'an lay deserted.

sentences.zh: 前滎陽太守高陵趙穀等招杏城盧水胡郝奴，帥戶四千入於長安，溫北皆應之，以穀為丞相。

translations.literal: Former Administrator of Xingyang Zhao Gu of Gaoling and others invited Hao Nu of the Lu River Hu at Xingcheng, who led four thousand households into Chang'an; all north of Wen responded, making Gu Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gu of Gaoling, former Administrator of Xingyang, and others summoned Hao Nu of the Lu River Hu at Xingcheng. He led four thousand households into Chang'an; the lands north of Wen rose with them, and Gu was made Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 扶風王穀有眾數千，保據馬嵬，奴遣弟多攻之。

translations.literal: Wang Gu of Fufeng had a host of several thousand holding Mawei; Nu sent his younger brother Duo to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gu of Fufeng held Mawei with several thousand men. Hao Nu sent his younger brother Duo to attack him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，後秦王萇自安定伐之，渭奔漢中。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Later Qin King Chang came from Anding to attack him; Gu fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Later Qin King Fu Chang marched from Anding against them. Wang Gu fled to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 萇執多而進，奴懼，請降，拜鎮北將軍、六谷大都督。

translations.literal: Chang seized Duo and advanced; Nu was afraid and requested surrender, and was appointed General Who Guards the North and Grand Director of the Six Valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Chang captured Duo and pressed forward. Nu, terrified, submitted and was appointed General Who Guards the North and Grand Director of the Six Valleys.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以尚書僕射陸納為左僕射，譙王恬為右僕射。

translations.literal: On guisi, Lu Na was made Left Vice Director and Prince of Qiao Tian was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Lu Na was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Prince of Qiao Tian Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 納，玩之子也。

translations.literal: Na was Wan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Na was the son of Lu Wan.

sentences.zh: 毛興襲擊王廣，敗之，廣奔秦州；

translations.literal: Mao Xing raided Wang Guang, defeated him, and Guang fled to Qinzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xing struck Wang Guang, routed him, and Guang fled to Qinzhou;

sentences.zh: 隴西鮮卑匹蘭執廣送後秦。

translations.literal: the Longxi Xianbei Pilan seized Guang and sent him to Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: the Longxi Xianbei chief Pilan seized Guang and delivered him to Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 興復欲攻王統於上邽，枹罕諸氐皆厭苦兵事，乃共殺興，推衛平為河州刺史，遣使請命於秦。

translations.literal: Xing again wished to attack Wang Tong at Shanggui; the Di of Fuhan all wearied of the hardships of war and jointly killed Xing, enthroning Wei Ping as regional inspector of Hezhou and sending an envoy to request appointment from Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Xing then planned to attack Wang Tong at Shanggui, but the Di of Fuhan, worn out by war, killed Xing together, raised Wei Ping as regional inspector of Hezhou, and sent envoys to Qin seeking confirmation.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂封其子農為遼西王，麟為趙王，隆為高陽王。

translations.literal: Yan King Chui enfeoffed his sons Nong as King of Liaoxi, Lin as King of Zhao, and Long as King of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan King Chui enfeoffed his sons: Nong as King of Liaoxi, Lin as King of Zhao, and Long as King of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 代王珪改稱魏王。

translations.literal: King Gui of Dai changed his title to King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: King Tuoba Gui took the title King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 張大豫自楊塢進屯姑臧城西，王穆及禿髮思復鞬子奚於帥眾三萬屯於城南；

translations.literal: Zhang Da Yu advanced from Yangwu to encamp west of Guzang city; Wang Mu and Tufa Sifu's son Xi Yu led thirty thousand troops to encamp south of the city;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Da Yu marched from Yangwu and encamped west of Guzang. Wang Mu and Xi Yu, son of Tufa Sifu, led thirty thousand men to camp south of the city;

sentences.zh: 呂光出擊，大破之，斬奚於等二萬餘級。

translations.literal: Lü Guang went out to attack, greatly defeated them, and beheaded Xi Yu and others—more than twenty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang sallied forth and routed them, taking the heads of Xi Yu and more than twenty thousand others.

sentences.zh: 秦大赦，以衛平為撫軍將軍、河州刺史，呂光為車騎大將軍、涼州牧。

translations.literal: Qin proclaimed a general amnesty, appointing Wei Ping as General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Hezhou, and Lü Guang as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin declared a general amnesty, making Wei Ping General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Hezhou, and Lü Guang Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 使者皆沒於後秦，不能達。

translations.literal: The envoys all were lost in Later Qin and could not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys were all cut off in Later Qin territory and never reached their destination.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂以范陽王德為尚書令，太原王楷為左僕射，樂浪王溫為司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Yan King Chui appointed Prince of Fanyang De as Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Taiyuan Kai as Left Vice Director, and Prince of Lelang Wen as Colonel-Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui appointed Prince De of Fanyang Director of the Secretariat, Prince Kai of Taiyuan Left Vice Director, and Prince Wen of Lelang Colonel-Director of Retainers.

sentences.zh: 後秦王萇即皇帝位於長安，大赦，改元建初，國號大秦。

translations.literal: Later Qin King Chang ascended the imperial throne at Chang'an, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Jianchu, and styled the state Great Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang of Later Qin took the imperial throne at Chang'an, declared a general amnesty, adopted the era name Jianchu, and proclaimed his state Great Qin.

sentences.zh: 追尊其父弋仲為景元皇帝，立妻蛇氏為皇后，子興為皇太子。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his father Yizhong as Emperor Jingyuan, installed his wife Lady She as empress, and his son Xing as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously ennobled his father Yizhong as Emperor Jingyuan, elevated his wife Lady She to empress, and named his son Xing crown prince.

sentences.zh: 置百官。

translations.literal: He installed the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: He established the full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 萇與群臣宴，酒酣，言曰：「諸卿皆與朕北面秦朝，今忽為君臣，得無恥乎！」

translations.literal: Chang feasted with his ministers; when the wine had gone deep, he said: "You all once faced north to serve Qin with me—now we are suddenly sovereign and subjects. Are we not ashamed!"
translations.idiomatic: At a feast with his ministers, Chang, well into his cups, remarked: "You all once served Qin at my side as subjects of another throne. Now suddenly we are sovereign and ministers—is there no shame in that?"

sentences.zh: 趙遷曰：「天不恥以陛下為子，臣等何恥為臣！」

translations.literal: Zhao Qian said: "Heaven is not ashamed to take Your Majesty as its son—why should we be ashamed to be your ministers!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qian replied: "If Heaven itself is not ashamed to claim Your Majesty as its chosen son, why should we blush to serve you as ministers?"

sentences.zh: 萇大笑。

translations.literal: Chang laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Chang roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪東如陵石，護佛侯部帥侯辰、乙佛部帥代題皆叛走。

translations.literal: King Gui of Wei went east to Lingshi; Huchen, leader of the Hufuhou tribe, and Daiti, leader of the Yifo tribe, both rebelled and fled.
translations.idiomatic: King Tuoba Gui of Wei traveled east to Lingshi. Huchen, chief of the Hufuhou tribe, and Daiti, chief of the Yifo tribe, both rebelled and fled.

sentences.zh: 諸將請追之，珪曰：「侯辰等累世服役，有罪且當忍之。

translations.literal: The generals asked to pursue them. Gui said: "Houchen and the others have served for generations—even if guilty, we ought to bear with them for now.
translations.idiomatic: The generals urged pursuit, but Gui said: "Houchen and his ilk have served us for generations. Even if they have wronged us, we ought to show forbearance.

sentences.zh: 方今國家草創，人情未壹，愚者固宜前卻，不足追也！」

translations.literal: Now the state is newly founded and hearts are not yet united—the foolish naturally advance and retreat; it is not worth pursuing them!"
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still being built from nothing, and loyalties are not yet settled. The foolish will naturally waver back and forth—it is scarcely worth chasing them down!"

sentences.zh: 六月，庚寅，以前輔國將軍楊亮為雍州刺史，鎮衛山陵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengyin, former General Who Assists the State Yang Liang was made Inspector of Yongzhou to guard and defend the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengyin, former General Who Assists the State Yang Liang was appointed Inspector of Yongzhou with charge over guarding the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史桓石民遣將軍晏謙擊弘農，下之。

translations.literal: Huan Shimin, Inspector of Jingzhou, sent General Yan Qian to attack Hongnong and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shimin, Inspector of Jingzhou, dispatched General Yan Qian against Hongnong and took the city.

sentences.zh: 初置湖、陝二戍。

translations.literal: For the first time the two garrisons of Hu and Shan were established.
translations.idiomatic: The garrisons at Hu and Shan were established for the first time.

sentences.zh: 西燕刁雲等殺西燕主忠，推慕容永為使持節、大都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、大單于、雍、秦、梁、涼四州牧、錄尚書事、河東王，稱籓於燕。

translations.literal: Diao Yun of Western Yan and others killed the ruler of Western Yan Zhong and enthroned Murong Yong as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commander of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, Governor of the four provinces Yong, Qin, Liang, and Liangzhou, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Hedong, paying allegiance to Yan as a vassal state.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yun and others of Western Yan assassinated the Western Yan ruler Murong Zhong and installed Murong Yong with full military and civil authority—as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commander of All Forces, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, Governor of Yong, Qin, Liang, and Liangzhou, with concurrent charge of the Secretariat, and as Prince of Hedong—while submitting to Yan as a tributary state.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂遣太原王楷、趙王麟、陳留王紹、章武王宙攻秦苻定、苻紹、苻謨、苻亮等；

translations.literal: Yan King Chui sent Prince of Taiyuan Kai, Prince of Zhao Lin, Prince of Chenliu Shao, and Prince of Zhangwu Zhou to attack Fu Ding, Fu Shao, Fu Mo, Fu Liang, and others of Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui dispatched Prince Kai of Taiyuan, Prince Lin of Zhao, Prince Shao of Chenliu, and Prince Zhou of Zhangwu to attack Fu Ding, Fu Shao, Fu Mo, Fu Liang, and other Qin commanders;

sentences.zh: 楷先以書與之，為陳禍福，定等皆降。

translations.literal: Kai first sent them a letter explaining fortune and disaster, and Ding and the others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Kai first wrote to them laying out the consequences of resistance and submission, and Fu Ding and his fellows all came over.

sentences.zh: 垂封定等為侯，曰：「以酬秦主之德。」

translations.literal: Chui enfeoffed Ding and the others as marquises, saying: "To repay the kindness of the Qin ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Chui enfeoffed them as marquises, declaring: "This is to repay the debt owed to the ruler of Qin."

sentences.zh: 秦主丕以都督中外諸軍事、司徒、錄尚書事王永為左丞相，太尉、東海王纂為大司馬，司空張蚝為太尉，尚書令咸陽徐義為司空，司隸校尉王騰為驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Qin King Pi appointed Wang Yong—Grand Commander of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Minister of Education, and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat—as Left Prime Minister; Fu Zuan, Grand Minister of War and Prince of Donghai, as Grand Marshal; Zhang Hao, Minister of Works, as Grand Minister of War; Xu Yi of Xianyang, Director of the Secretariat, as Minister of Works; and Wang Teng, Colonel-Director of Retainers, as General of Cavalry on the Left and with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi reorganized his court: Wang Yong became Left Prime Minister with his existing posts as Grand Commander and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat; Prince Fu Zuan of Donghai became Grand Marshal; Zhang Hao was promoted from Minister of Works to Grand Minister of War; Xu Yi of Xianyang moved from Director of the Secretariat to Minister of Works; and Wang Teng, Colonel-Director of Retainers, was made General of Cavalry on the Left with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 永傳檄四方公侯、牧守、壘主、民豪，共討姚萇、慕容垂，令各帥所統，以孟冬上旬會大駕於臨晉。

translations.literal: Yong circulated a proclamation to the four directions—to princes, marquises, governors, garrison commanders, and local magnates—calling on them jointly to attack Yao Chang and Murong Chui, ordering each to lead his forces and in the first ten days of mid-winter assemble with the imperial carriage at Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong issued a call to arms across the realm, summoning princes, governors, garrison captains, and local strongmen to join in punishing Yao Chang and Murong Chui. Each was to lead his own forces and rendezvous with the emperor at Linjin in the first third of the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 於是天水姜延、馮翊寇明、河東王昭、新平張晏、京兆杜敏、扶風馬朗、建忠將軍、高平牧官都尉扶風王敏等鹹承檄起兵，各有眾數萬，遣使詣秦，丕皆就拜將軍、郡守，封列侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiang Yan of Tianshui, Kou Ming of Fengyi, Wang Zhao of Hedong, Zhang Yan of Xinping, Du Min of Jingzhao, Ma Lang of Fufeng, General Who Establishes Loyalty Wang Min of Fufeng—Chief Commandant of the Pasturage Office of Gaoping—all received the proclamation and raised troops, each with a following of several tens of thousands. They sent envoys to Qin, and Pi on the spot invested them as generals, prefects, and enfeoffed them as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: At once Jiang Yan of Tianshui, Kou Ming of Fengyi, Wang Zhao of Hedong, Zhang Yan of Xinping, Du Min of Jingzhao, Ma Lang of Fufeng, General Who Establishes Loyalty Wang Min of Fufeng (Chief Commandant of the Pasturage Office of Gaoping), and others answered the call. Each raised a force of tens of thousands, sent envoys to Qin, and received on-the-spot appointments as generals and prefects, with enfeoffment as marquises.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍鄧景擁眾五千據彭池，與竇沖為首尾，以擊後秦。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the Champions Deng Jing, with a following of five thousand, held Pengchi, coordinating with Dou Chong in pincer fashion to strike Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the Champions Deng Jing mustered five thousand men and seized Pengchi, coordinating with Dou Chong in a pincer to strike Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 丕以景為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Pi made Jing Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Pi appointed Deng Jing Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 景，羌之子也。

translations.literal: Jing was Qiang's son.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jing was the son of Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇徙安定五千餘戶於長安。

translations.literal: Later Qin King Chang relocated more than five thousand households from Anding to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang relocated more than five thousand Anding households to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，秦平涼太守金熙、安定都尉沒弈干與後秦左將軍姚方成戰於孫丘谷，方成兵敗。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Jin Xi, Administrator of Pingliang in Qin, and Muyigan, Commandant of Anding, fought with Yao Fangcheng, Left General of Later Qin, at Sunqiu Valley. Fangcheng's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Qin's Administrator of Pingliang Jin Xi and Anding Commandant Muyigan fought Later Qin's Left General Yao Fangcheng at Sunqiu Valley and routed him.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇以其弟征虜將軍緒為司隸校尉，鎮長安；

translations.literal: Later Qin King Chang made his younger brother Xu, General Who Punishes Captives, Colonel-Director of Retainers and stationed him to guard Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang appointed his brother Yao Xu, General Who Punishes Captives, Colonel-Director of Retainers and left him to hold Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 自將至安定擊熙等，大破之。

translations.literal: he personally led troops to Anding to attack Xi and the others and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: then personally marched to Anding, struck Xi and his allies, and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 金熙本東胡之種；

translations.literal: Jin Xi was originally of Eastern Hu stock;
translations.idiomatic: Jin Xi was of Eastern Hu origin;

sentences.zh: 沒弈干，鮮卑多蘭部帥也。

translations.literal: Muyigan was leader of the Xianbei Duolan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Muyigan was chief of the Xianbei Duolan tribe.

sentences.zh: 枹罕諸氐以衛平衰老，難為成功，議廢之，而憚其宗強，累日不決。

translations.literal: The Di of Bohan, because Wei Ping was old and success would be hard to achieve, discussed deposing him, but feared the strength of his clan and for days could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Di leaders at Bohan concluded that Wei Ping's age made victory unlikely and debated replacing him, yet they feared the power of his clan and deliberated for days without resolution.

sentences.zh: 氐啖青謂諸將曰：「大事宜時定，不然，變生。

translations.literal: The Di chieftain Dan Qing told the generals: "Great affairs should be settled in timely fashion—otherwise trouble will arise.
translations.idiomatic: The Di leader Dan Qing told the commanders: "A matter this weighty must be settled now, or disorder will follow.

sentences.zh: 諸君但請衛公為會，觀我所為。」

translations.literal: You need only invite Lord Wei to a gathering and watch what I do."
translations.idiomatic: Simply invite Lord Wei to a banquet and watch what I do."

sentences.zh: 會七夕大宴，青抽劍而前曰：「今天下大亂，吾曹休戚同之，非賢主不可以濟大事。

translations.literal: On the Qixi festival they held a great feast. Qing drew his sword and stepped forward, saying: "Today the realm is in great chaos; we share fortune and woe alike—without a worthy sovereign great affairs cannot be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: At the Double Seventh festival they held a grand banquet. Qing drew his sword and stepped forward: "The empire is in chaos, and we rise or fall together. Without a worthy ruler we cannot see this through.

sentences.zh: 衛公老，宜返初服以避賢路。

translations.literal: Lord Wei is old; he ought to return to private life and yield the path to the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Wei is old; he should retire to private life and make way for better men.

sentences.zh: 狄道長苻登，雖王室疏屬，志略雄明，請共立之，以赴大駕。

translations.literal: Fu Deng, Prefect of Didao, though a distant member of the royal house, has heroic resolve and clear strategy. I ask that we jointly install him and march to join the imperial host.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng, prefect of Didao, is only a distant kinsman of the house of Qin, but his ability and ambition are outstanding. I propose we install him and march east to answer the emperor's call.

sentences.zh: 諸君有不同者，即下異議！」

translations.literal: If any among you disagree, speak your dissent at once!"
translations.idiomatic: If anyone here disagrees, say so now!"

sentences.zh: 乃奮劍攘袂，將斬異己者。

translations.literal: He then flourished his sword and rolled up his sleeves, ready to cut down any who dissented.
translations.idiomatic: He swept his sleeves back and brandished his sword, poised to strike down anyone who objected.

sentences.zh: 眾皆從之，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: All complied; none dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone fell in line; no one dared meet his eye.

sentences.zh: 於是推登為使持節、都督隴右諸軍事、撫軍大將軍、雍、河二州牧、略陽公，帥眾五萬，東下隴，攻南安，拔之，馳使請命於秦。

translations.literal: Thereupon they enthroned Deng as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs west of Long, General Who Pacifies the Army, Governor of Yong and He provinces, Duke of Lueyang; he led fifty thousand troops east down Long, attacked Nan'an, captured it, and dispatched a fast courier to request orders from Qin.
translations.idiomatic: They then invested Fu Deng as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Forces west of Long, General Who Pacifies the Army, Governor of Yong and He, and Duke of Lueyang. At the head of fifty thousand men he marched east off the Long plateau, took Nan'an, and sent urgent word to Qin requesting confirmation of his authority.

sentences.zh: 登，秦主丕族子也。

translations.literal: Deng was a clansman of Qin King Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng was a kinsman of Fu Pi.

sentences.zh: 祕宜與莫侯悌眷帥其眾三萬餘戶降於乞伏國仁，國仁拜宜東秦州刺史，悌眷梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Mi Yi and Mohe Tikuan led their following of more than thirty thousand households in surrender to Qifu Guoren; Guoren appointed Yi Governor of Eastern Qinzhou and Tikuan Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Yi and Mohe Tikuan brought more than thirty thousand households over to Qifu Guoren, who made Yi Governor of Eastern Qinzhou and Tikuan Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 已酉，魏王珪還盛樂，代題復以部落來降，十餘日，又奔劉顯；

translations.literal: On jiyou, King Gui of Wei returned to Shengle. Daiti again came with his tribe to surrender; after ten-odd days he again fled to Liu Xian;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou King Tuoba Gui returned to Shengle. Daiti once again submitted with his tribe, but within a fortnight he had fled to Liu Xian.

sentences.zh: 珪使其孫倍斥代領其眾。

translations.literal: Gui had his grandson Beichi take over leading their following.
translations.idiomatic: Gui put his grandson Beichi in command of Daiti's people.

sentences.zh: 劉顯弟肺泥帥眾降魏。

translations.literal: Liu Xian's younger brother Feini led his following in surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian's brother Feini submitted to Wei with his followers.

sentences.zh: 八月，燕主垂留太子寶守中山，以趙王麟為尚書右僕射，錄留台。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Yan King Chui left Crown Prince Bao to guard Zhongshan and made Prince of Zhao Lin Right Vice Director of the Secretariat with charge of the rear capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Murong Chui left Crown Prince Bao to hold Zhongshan and appointed Prince Lin of Zhao Right Vice Director of the Secretariat with charge of the rear administration.

sentences.zh: 庚午，自帥范陽王德等南略地，使高陽王隆東徇平原。

translations.literal: On gengwu he personally led Prince of Fanyang De and others south to seize territory, and sent Prince of Gaoyang Long east to sweep the Pingyuan region.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he personally led Prince De of Fanyang and others on a southern campaign while dispatching Prince Long of Gaoyang east to subdue the Pingyuan region.

sentences.zh: 丁零鮮于乞保曲陽西山，聞垂南伐，出營望都，剽掠居民。

translations.literal: Xianyu Qi of the Dingling, holding the western hills of Quyang, heard that Chui was campaigning south, came out of camp at Wangdu, and plundered the populace.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Qi of the Dingling, encamped in the western hills of Quyang, heard Murong Chui was marching south. He moved his camp to Wangdu and pillaged the countryside.

sentences.zh: 趙王麟自出討之，諸將皆曰：「殿下虛鎮遠征，萬一無功而返，虧損威重，不如遣諸將討之。」

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Lin personally went out to suppress him. The generals all said: "Your Highness would leave the rear capital undefended to campaign far away—if you return without success your prestige will suffer. Better to send the generals to subdue him."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lin set out in person to suppress him, but his officers objected: "If Your Highness leaves the capital empty to campaign afar and returns empty-handed, your authority will suffer. Better to send the generals."

sentences.zh: 麟曰：「乞聞大駕在外，無所畏忌，必不設備，一舉可取，不足憂也。」

translations.literal: Lin said: "Qi will hear that the imperial host is abroad and feel freed of all restraint—he will surely make no preparations. One stroke can take him; there is nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: Lin replied: "Qi will hear the emperor is away and think himself untouchable. He won't be on guard—we can take him in one strike. There's nothing to fret over.

sentences.zh: 乃聲言至魯口，夜，回趣乞，比明，至其營；

translations.literal: He then announced he was going to Lukou; by night he doubled back toward Qi, and by dawn reached his camp;
translations.idiomatic: He announced a march on Lukou, then under cover of night wheeled about toward Qi and reached his camp by daybreak;

sentences.zh: 掩擊，擒之。

translations.literal: struck by surprise and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: fell on him by surprise and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 翟遼寇譙，朱序擊走之。

translations.literal: Zhai Liao raided Qiao; Zhu Xu struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao raided Qiao, and Zhu Xu beat him back.

sentences.zh: 秦主丕以苻登為征西大將軍、開府儀同三司、南安王，持節、州牧、都督，皆因其所稱而授之。

translations.literal: Qin King Pi made Fu Deng General Who Campaigns West, with privilege to open an office and rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and Prince of Nan'an; Bearer of the Staff, Governor, and Commander—all titles conferred according to what he had already claimed for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi confirmed Fu Deng in the titles he had already assumed—General Who Campaigns West, privilege of an independent command equal to the Three Excellencies, Prince of Nan'an, Bearer of the Staff, provincial governor, and military commander.

sentences.zh: 又以徐義為右丞相。

translations.literal: He also made Xu Yi Right Prime Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Xu Yi Right Prime Minister.

sentences.zh: 留王騰守晉陽，右僕射楊輔戍壺關，帥眾四萬，進屯平陽。

translations.literal: He left Wang Teng to guard Jinyang and Yang Fu, Right Vice Director, to garrison Huguan; he led forty thousand troops and advanced to encamp at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Teng was left to hold Jinyang, Yang Fu to garrison Huguan, and Pi himself led forty thousand men to encamp at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 初，後秦主萇之弟碩德統所部羌居隴上，聞萇起兵，自稱征西將軍，聚眾於冀城以應之；

translations.literal: Earlier, Shude, younger brother of Later Qin King Chang, commanding the Di under him dwelling on Long, upon hearing that Chang had raised troops styled himself General Who Campaigns West and gathered a force at Jicheng to respond;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yao Shude, Chang's younger brother, had been leading their Di followers on the Long plateau. When Chang rose in rebellion Shude declared himself General Who Campaigns West and raised a force at Jicheng in support;

sentences.zh: 以兄孫詳為安遠將軍，據隴城，從孫訓為安西將軍，據南安之赤亭，與秦秦州刺史王統相持。

translations.literal: he made his elder brother's grandson Xiang General Who Pacifies the Distances and hold Longcheng, and his younger brother's grandson Xun General Who Pacifies the West and hold Chiting in Nan'an, locked in stalemate with Wang Tong, Inspector of Qinzhou of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He placed his elder brother's grandson Xiang at Longcheng as General Who Pacifies the Distances, and his younger brother's grandson Xun at Chiting in Nan'an as General Who Pacifies the West, where they locked horns with Wang Tong, Qin's Inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 萇自安定引兵會碩德攻統，天水屠各、略陽羌胡應之者一萬餘戶，秦略陽太守王皮降之。

translations.literal: Chang led troops from Anding to join Shude in attacking Tong; more than ten thousand households of Tuge and Qiang-Hu of Tianshui and Lueyang responded, and Wang Pi, Administrator of Lueyang in Qin, surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang marched from Anding to join Shude against Wang Tong. More than ten thousand Tuge and Qiang-Hu households of Tianshui and Lueyang rallied to them, and Qin's Administrator of Lueyang Wang Pi submitted.

sentences.zh: 初，秦滅代，遷代王什翼犍少子窟咄於長安，從慕容永東徙，永以窟咄為新興太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qin destroyed Dai, the youngest son of King Shijian of Dai, Kutou, was moved to Chang'an; following Murong Yong's eastward migration, Yong made Kutou Administrator of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin had overthrown Dai, Dai's King Shijian's youngest son Kutou had been relocated to Chang'an. When Murong Yong moved east, he made Kutou Administrator of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 劉顯遣其弟亢泥迎窟咄，以兵隨之，逼魏南境，諸部騷動。

translations.literal: Liu Xian sent his younger brother Kangni to welcome Kutou, with troops following him, pressing on Wei's southern border; the various tribes were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian sent his brother Kangni to bring Kutou back with an army, pressing the southern Wei frontier and throwing the tribes into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪左右於桓等與部人謀執珪以應窟咄，幢將代人莫題等亦潛與窟咄交通。

translations.literal: Attendants of King Gui of Wei such as Yu Huan and others plotted with tribesmen to seize Gui and respond to Kutou; Mo Ti of Dai and other standard-bearer chiefs also secretly communicated with Kutou.
translations.idiomatic: Among Tuoba Gui's own court, Yu Huan and others conspired with tribal leaders to seize the king and join Kutou. Mo Ti of Dai and other standard-bearer chiefs were also secretly in contact with him.

sentences.zh: 桓舅穆崇告之，珪誅桓等五人，莫題等七姓悉原不問。

translations.literal: Huan's maternal uncle Mu Chong reported this; Gui executed Huan and four others—five men in all—and completely pardoned the seven clans including Mo Ti without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan's uncle Mu Chong exposed the plot. Gui executed Yu Huan and four co-conspirators, but fully pardoned Mo Ti's clan and six allied lines without further investigation.

sentences.zh: 珪懼內難，北逾阻山，復依賀蘭部，遣外朝大人遼東安同求救於燕，燕主垂遣趙王麟救之。

translations.literal: Gui, fearing internal strife, crossed north over Zushan and again relied on the Helan tribe; he sent Outer Court Grandee An Tong of Liaodong to seek rescue from Yan, and Yan King Chui sent Prince of Zhao Lin to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful of civil war, Gui fled north over Zushan and took refuge again with the Helan tribe. He sent Outer Court Grandee An Tong of Liaodong to beg aid from Yan, and Murong Chui dispatched Prince Lin of Zhao to his relief.

sentences.zh: 九月，王統以秦州降於後秦。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wang Tong surrendered Qinzhou to Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Tong surrendered Qinzhou to Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇以姚碩德為使持節、都督隴右諸軍事、秦州刺史，鎮上邽。

translations.literal: Later Qin King Chang made Yao Shude Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs west of Long, Inspector of Qinzhou, stationed at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang appointed Yao Shude Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Forces west of Long, and Inspector of Qinzhou, with his seat at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 呂光得秦王堅凶問，舉軍縞素，謚曰文昭皇帝。

translations.literal: Lü Guang received news of King Fu Jian of Qin's violent death; the whole army wore white mourning and posthumously honored him as Emperor Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: On receiving word of Fu Jian's murder, Lü Guang put the entire army in mourning and posthumously honored him as Emperor Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，大赦，改元大安。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he declared a general amnesty and adopted the era name Da'an.

sentences.zh: 西燕慕容永遣使詣秦主丕，求假道東歸。

translations.literal: Murong Yong of Western Yan sent envoys to Qin King Pi requesting passage eastward to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong of Western Yan sent envoys to Fu Pi requesting safe passage eastward to return home.

sentences.zh: 丕弗許，與永戰於襄陵，秦兵大敗，左丞相王永、衛大將軍俱石子皆死。

translations.literal: Pi refused; he fought Yong at Xiangling. Qin troops suffered a great defeat; Left Prime Minister Wang Yong and Guardian General Ju Shizi both died.
translations.idiomatic: Pi refused. At Xiangling he fought Yong and suffered catastrophic defeat; Left Prime Minister Wang Yong and Guardian General Ju Shizi were both killed.

sentences.zh: 初，東海王纂自長安來，麾下壯士三千餘人，丕忌之，既敗，懼為纂所殺，帥騎數千南奔東垣，謀襲洛陽。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince Fu Zuan of Donghai had come from Chang'an with more than three thousand stalwart warriors under his command. Pi was jealous of him. After the defeat, fearing Zuan would kill him, Pi led several thousand horsemen south fleeing to Dongyuan, plotting to seize Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fu Zuan of Donghai had arrived from Chang'an with over three thousand seasoned fighters, and Pi had been wary of him. After the rout, Pi feared Zuan would kill him. He fled south to Dongyuan with several thousand cavalry, intending to strike at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 揚威將軍馮該自陝邀擊之，殺丕，執其太子寧、長樂王壽送建康；

translations.literal: General Who Displays Might Feng Gai intercepted him from Shan, killed Pi, seized his Crown Prince Ning and Prince of Changle Shou and sent them to Jiankang;
translations.idiomatic: General Who Displays Might Feng Gai intercepted him at Shan, killed Pi, captured Crown Prince Ning and Prince Shou of Changle, and sent them to Jiankang;

sentences.zh: 詔赦不誅，以付苻宏。

translations.literal: an edict pardoned them from execution and handed them over to Fu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict spared their lives and placed them in Fu Hong's custody.

sentences.zh: 纂與其弟尚書永平侯師奴帥秦眾數萬走據杏城，其餘王公百官皆沒於永。

translations.literal: Zuan and his younger brother Shiniu, Minister and Marquis of Yongping, led several tens of thousands of Qin followers in flight to seize and hold Xingcheng; the remaining princes, nobles, and officials were all lost to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan and his brother Shiniu, a minister and Marquis of Yongping, fled with tens of thousands of Qin loyalists and seized Xingcheng. The rest of the court—princes, nobles, and officials—fell into Yong's hands.

sentences.zh: 永遂進據長子，即皇帝位，改元中興。

translations.literal: Yong then advanced to seize and hold Changzi, ascended the imperial throne, and changed the era name to Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yong pressed on to Changzi, took the imperial throne, and proclaimed the era name Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 將以秦後楊氏為上夫人，楊氏引劍刺永，為永所殺。

translations.literal: He intended to make Lady Yang, former empress of Qin, his Senior Lady. Lady Yang drew a sword to stab Yong and was killed by Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to take Lady Yang, Fu Jian's former empress, as his Senior Consort. She drew a sword to assassinate him; Yong killed her.

sentences.zh: 甲申，海西公弈薨於吳。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the Duke of Haixi Yi died at Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Duke Yi of Haixi died at Wu.

sentences.zh: 燕寺人吳深據清河反，燕主垂攻之，不克。
