translations.literal: The eunuch Wu Shen of Yan held Qinghe in rebellion; Yan King Chui attacked him but could not capture him.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan eunuch Wu Shen rebelled and seized Qinghe. Murong Chui attacked him but failed to take the city.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇還安定。

translations.literal: Later Qin King Chang returned to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang returned to Anding.

sentences.zh: 秦南安王登既克南安，夷、夏歸之者三萬餘戶，遂進攻姚碩德於秦州，後秦主萇自往救之。

translations.literal: Prince Fu Deng of Nan'an of Qin, having already captured Nan'an, with Barbarian and Han submitters numbering more than thirty thousand households, then advanced to attack Yao Shude at Qinzhou; Later Qin King Chang personally went to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: After seizing Nan'an, Fu Deng, Prince of Nan'an, drew more than thirty thousand Yi and Han households to his banner and marched on Yao Shude at Qinzhou. Fu Chang hurried to the rescue in person.

sentences.zh: 登與萇戰於胡奴阜，大破之，斬首二萬餘級，將軍啖青射萇，中之。

translations.literal: Deng fought Chang at Hunufu, greatly defeated him, cut off more than twenty thousand heads, and General Dan Qing shot Chang and hit him.
translations.idiomatic: At Hunufu, Deng routed Chang's army, taking more than twenty thousand heads. General Dan Qing shot Chang and struck him.

sentences.zh: 萇創重，走保上邽，姚碩德代之統眾。

translations.literal: Chang's wound was severe; he fled to hold Shanggui, and Yao Shude took his place commanding the host.
translations.idiomatic: Badly wounded, Chang withdrew into Shanggui and left Yao Shude to command the army.

sentences.zh: 燕趙王麟軍未至魏，拓跋窟咄稍前逼魏王珪，賀染干侵魏北部以應之。

translations.literal: Before Prince of Zhao Lin's army of Yan reached Wei, Tuoba Kutou gradually pressed forward against King Tuoba Gui of Wei; He Rangan invaded Wei's northern region in response.
translations.idiomatic: Before Prince Lin's Yan forces could reach Wei, Kutou was already pressing Tuoba Gui, while He Rangan raided the northern Wei frontier in support.

sentences.zh: 魏眾驚擾，北部大人叔孫普洛亡奔劉衛辰。

translations.literal: Wei's masses were alarmed and shaken; the Northern Great Chieftain Shusun Pulo fled to Liu Weichen.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through Wei's ranks. Shusun Pulo, the Northern Great Chieftain, defected to Liu Weichen.

sentences.zh: 麟聞之，遽遣安同等歸。

translations.literal: Lin heard of this and hastily sent An Tong and others back.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin heard, he immediately sent An Tong back with his force.

sentences.zh: 魏人知燕軍在近，眾心少安。

translations.literal: The people of Wei, knowing Yan's army was near, were somewhat reassured in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yan's army was close at hand, Wei's people regained some measure of calm.

sentences.zh: 窟咄進屯高柳，珪引兵與麟會擊之，窟咄大敗，奔劉衛辰，衛辰殺之。

translations.literal: Kutou advanced to encamp at Gaoliu. Gui led troops to join Lin in attacking him. Kutou suffered a great defeat, fled to Liu Weichen, and Weichen killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Kutou encamped at Gaoliu. Gui joined forces with Lin and crushed him. Kutou fled to Liu Weichen, who had him killed.

sentences.zh: 珪悉收其眾，以代人庫狄干為北部大人。

translations.literal: Gui fully absorbed his following and made Kudi Gan of Dai Northern Great Chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Gui absorbed Kutou's entire following and appointed Kudi Gan of Dai Northern Great Chieftain.

sentences.zh: 麟引兵還中山。

translations.literal: Lin led his troops back to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin withdrew his army to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 劉衛辰居朔方，士馬甚盛。

translations.literal: Liu Weichen dwelt in Shuofang; his warriors and horses were very plentiful.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weichen held Shuofang, with formidable armies and horse herds.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇以衛辰為大將軍、大單于、河西王、幽州牧，西燕主永以衛辰為大將軍、朔州牧。

translations.literal: Later Qin King Chang made Weichen Grand General, Grand Chanyu, Prince of Hexi, and Governor of Youzhou; Western Yan King Yong made Weichen Grand General and Governor of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang invested Weichen as Grand General, Grand Chanyu, Prince of Hexi, and Governor of Youzhou, while Murong Yong of Western Yan made him Grand General and Governor of Shuozhou—the same man courted by two rival thrones.

sentences.zh: 十一月，秦尚書寇遺奉勃海王懿、濟北王昶自杏城奔南安，南安王登發喪行服，謚秦主丕曰哀平皇帝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Kou Yi, Minister of Qin, escorting Prince of Bohai Yi and Prince of Jibei Chang, fled from Xingcheng to Nan'an. Prince Deng of Nan'an issued mourning and wore mourning garments, posthumously honoring Qin King Pi as Emperor Aiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Minister Kou Yi of Qin escorted Princes Yi of Bohai and Chang of Jibei from Xingcheng to Nan'an. Fu Deng proclaimed mourning rites and posthumously honored Fu Pi as Emperor Aiping.

sentences.zh: 登議立懿為主，眾曰：「勃海王雖先帝之子，然年在幼沖，未堪多難。

translations.literal: Deng discussed installing Yi as ruler. The assembly said: "Though the Prince of Bohai is the late emperor's son, his years are young and tender—he cannot bear the many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Deng proposed enthroning Prince Yi, but the assembly objected: "Prince Yi may be the late emperor's son, but he is still a child and not equal to these troubles.

sentences.zh: 今三虜窺覦，宜立長君，非大王不可。」

translations.literal: Now three enemies eye us covetously; an elder ruler ought to be installed—none but Your Highness will do."
translations.idiomatic: Three foes are watching us with hungry eyes. We need a seasoned ruler—and only Your Highness will serve."

sentences.zh: 登乃為壇於隴東，即皇帝位，大赦，改元太初，大置百官。

translations.literal: Deng then built an altar east of Long, ascended the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Taichu, and installed many officials.
translations.idiomatic: Deng erected an altar east of Long, took the throne, declared a general amnesty, adopted the era name Taichu, and established his full court.

sentences.zh: 慕容柔、慕容盛及盛弟會皆在長子，盛謂柔、會曰：「主上已中興幽、冀，東西未壹，吾屬居嫌疑之地，為智為愚，皆將不免。

translations.literal: Murong Rou, Murong Sheng, and Sheng's younger brother Hui were all at Changzi. Sheng said to Rou and Hui: "Our lord has already restored Yan in You and Ji, yet east and west are not yet united. We dwell in a place of suspicion—whether wise or foolish, none of us will escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Rou, Murong Sheng, and Sheng's younger brother Hui were all at Changzi. Sheng told Rou and Hui: "Our lord has revived Yan in You and Ji, but the realm is still divided. We stand under suspicion here—clever or dull, none of us is safe.

sentences.zh: 不若以時東歸，無為坐待魚肉也。」

translations.literal: Would it not be better to return east in good time, rather than sit and wait to become fish and meat?"
translations.idiomatic: Better to return east while we still can, rather than sit here waiting to be carved up like fish on a board."

sentences.zh: 遂相與亡歸燕。

translations.literal: Thereupon they fled together back to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they fled together back to Yan.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，西燕主永悉誅燕主俊及燕主垂之子孫，男女無遺。

translations.literal: More than a year later, the Western Yan ruler Murong Yong executed all the descendants, male and female without exception, of Yan ruler Murong Jun and Yan ruler Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, Western Yan ruler Murong Yong executed every descendant, male and female without exception, of Yan rulers Murong Jun and Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 張大豫自西郡入臨洮，掠民五千餘戶，保據俱城。

translations.literal: Zhang Dayu entered Lintao from Xijun, plundered more than five thousand households of the people, and held Jucheng as a strongpoint.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dayu entered Lintao from Xijun, plundered more than five thousand households, and fortified himself at Jucheng.

sentences.zh: 十二月，呂光自稱使持節、侍中、中外大都督、督隴右、河西諸軍事、大將軍、涼州牧、酒泉公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Lü Guang styled himself Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Commander-in-Chief of All Affairs Within and Without, Director of Military Affairs for Longyou and Hexi, Grand General, Inspector of Liangzhou, and Duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Lü Guang styled himself Bearer of the Staff of Authority, palace attendant, grand commander-in-chief of all affairs within and without, director of military affairs for Longyou and Hexi, grand general, inspector of Liangzhou, and Duke of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 秦主登立世祖神主於軍中，載以輜軿，建黃旗青蓋，以虎賁三百人衛之，凡所欲為，必啟主而後行。

translations.literal: King Fu Deng of Qin set up the spirit tablet of Emperor Shizu in the army camp, carried it in a covered carriage, raised a yellow banner and green canopy, and guarded it with three hundred tiger guards; whatever he wished to do, he had to report to the spirit lord before acting.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Deng set up the spirit tablet of Emperor Shizu in camp, carried it in a covered carriage under a yellow banner and green canopy, and posted three hundred tiger guards around it; whatever he wished to do, he first reported to the spirit lord.

sentences.zh: 引兵五萬，東擊後秦，將士皆刻鉾、鎧為「死」「休」字；

translations.literal: He led fifty thousand troops east to attack Later Qin; officers and soldiers all carved their spears and armor with the characters "death" and "rest";
translations.idiomatic: He led fifty thousand troops east against Later Qin; officers and soldiers carved their spears and armor with the characters for "death" and "rest";

sentences.zh: 每戰以劍槊為方圓大陣，知有厚薄，從中分配，故人自為戰，所向無前。

translations.literal: in every battle he formed a great square or round array with swords and spears, knew where strength was thick or thin, and assigned men accordingly from the center, so each man fought for himself and wherever they went none could stand before them.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he formed a great square or round array with swords and spears, knew where the line was strong or weak, and assigned men accordingly from the center, so each man fought for himself and wherever they went none could stand before them.

sentences.zh: 初，長安之將敗也，中壘將軍徐嵩、屯騎校尉胡空各聚眾五千，結壘自固；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chang'an was about to fall, Central Rampart General Xu Song and Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry Hu Kong each gathered five thousand followers and built stockades to hold themselves secure;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Chang'an was about to fall, Central Rampart General Xu Song and Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry Hu Kong each gathered five thousand followers and built stockades to hold themselves secure;

sentences.zh: 既而受後秦官爵。

translations.literal: they then accepted offices and ranks from Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: they then accepted offices and ranks from Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇以王禮葬秦主堅於二壘之間。

translations.literal: Later Qin ruler Yao Chang buried King Fu Jian of Qin between the two stockades with the rites due a king.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin ruler Yao Chang buried King Fu Jian between the two stockades with the rites due a king.

sentences.zh: 及登至，嵩、空以眾降之。

translations.literal: When Deng arrived, Song and Kong surrendered their followers to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng arrived, Song and Kong surrendered their followers to him.

sentences.zh: 登拜嵩雍州刺史，空京兆尹，改葬堅以天子之禮。

translations.literal: Deng appointed Song Inspector of Yongzhou and Kong Intendant of Jingzhao, and reburied Fu Jian with the rites due the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Deng appointed Song inspector of Yongzhou and Kong intendant of Jingzhao, and reburied Fu Jian with the rites due the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，燕主垂攻吳深壘，拔之，深單馬走。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Yan ruler Murong Chui attacked Wu Shen's stockade, took it, and Shen fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Yan ruler Murong Chui attacked Wu Shen's stockade, took it, and Shen fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 垂進屯聊城之逢關陂。

translations.literal: Chui advanced and encamped at Fengguanpo in Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chui advanced and encamped at Fengguanpo in Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 初，燕太子洗馬溫詳來奔，以為濟北太守，屯東阿。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yan Crown Prince's Groom of the Stables Wen Xiang had come over in surrender; Chui made him Administrator of Jibei and stationed him at Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yan crown prince's Groom of the Stables Wen Xiang had come over in surrender; Chui made him administrator of Jibei and stationed him at Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂遣范陽王德、高陽王隆攻之，詳遣從弟攀守河南岸，子楷守碻磝以拒之。

translations.literal: Yan ruler Murong Chui sent Prince of Fanyang De and Prince of Gaoyang Long to attack him; Xiang sent his younger cousin from the collateral line Pan to hold the south bank of the Yellow River and his son Kai to hold Que'ao to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ruler Murong Chui sent Prince of Fanyang De and Prince of Gaoyang Long to attack him; Xiang sent his younger cousin Pan to hold the south bank of the Yellow River and his son Kai to hold Que'ao to resist them.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂以魏王珪為西單于，封上谷王，珪不受。

translations.literal: Yan ruler Murong Chui made King of Wei Gui Western Chanyu and enfeoffed him as King of Shanggu; Gui did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ruler Murong Chui made King of Wei Gui Western Chanyu and enfeoffed him as King of Shanggu, but Gui did not accept.
